title: Midjourney Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Is Midjourney worth paying for in 2026? A hands-on look at its pricing tiers, standout features, and where it falls short.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Midjourney worth it in 2026?

Midjourney is one of the two or three AI image generators most creators default to, and for good reason: its outputs tend to have a distinct, painterly polish that other generators struggle to match straight out of the box. It's genuinely good, but it's also Discord/web-only, has no permanent free tier, and its command-based workflow has a real learning curve — so whether it's worth it depends heavily on how often you generate images and whether you need pixel-precise control.

### At a glance

| | Midjourney |
| --- | --- |
| Starting price | $10/month (Basic Plan, billed monthly) |
| Free tier/trial | No ongoing free tier; free trials are rarely available and often disabled due to abuse |
| Best for | Concept art, illustration, mood boards, marketing visuals, stylized creative work |
| Standout feature | Consistently strong default aesthetic quality, plus style/character reference tools |

## What Midjourney actually is

Midjourney is an independent research lab and AI image-generation service, self-funded and notably not backed by the usual big-tech investors that fund most other frontier AI labs. It generates images from text prompts (and now image inputs too) using its own proprietary diffusion models, iterated through several major versions — V4, V5.x, V6/V6.1, and the V7 and V8-series models that followed through 2025 and into 2026 — alongside specialized "Niji" versions tuned for anime and illustrated styles. Midjourney doesn't publish detailed architecture papers the way some competitors do, so specifics of the current model are known mainly through its own release notes rather than an academic paper.

Originally, the only way to use Midjourney was through Discord, typing `/imagine` commands into a bot and getting a 2x2 grid of images back. That's still supported, but since mid-2024 Midjourney has also offered its own web app with image editing, panning, zooming, region-based variation, and inpainting — now the more common way most subscribers actually work. There's still no official standalone desktop or mobile app; everything runs through a browser tab or Discord.

## Pricing

Midjourney sells access as a flat monthly or annual subscription rather than per-image credits, though heavier tiers effectively function as more generation time. As of Midjourney's own published plan structure, the tiers break down roughly like this:

| Plan | Monthly price | Annual price (per month, billed yearly) | Fast GPU time | Relax mode | Stealth mode |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Basic | $10 | ~$8 | ~3.3 hours/month | Not included | Not included |
| Standard | $30 | ~$24 | ~15 hours/month | Unlimited | Not included |
| Pro | $60 | ~$48 | ~30 hours/month | Unlimited | Included |
| Mega | $120 | ~$96 | ~60 hours/month | Unlimited | Included |

"Fast" hours are the GPU time used to generate images at normal speed; once you burn through your allotment, jobs either queue in slower "relax" mode (unlimited on Standard and above) or you buy extra fast-hours on top. Stealth mode, only on Pro and Mega, keeps your generations off the public community feed — useful for client work you don't want showing up in a public gallery search. All paid plans include commercial usage rights, though Midjourney's terms carve out extra requirements for companies above a certain revenue threshold, worth reading directly on its terms-of-service page if you're generating for a larger company.

Pricing, free-tier availability and feature allotments above were accurate as of this post's publish date but Midjourney has changed its plan structure before (it dropped free trials entirely in 2023, then briefly experimented with limited ones again) — always confirm current numbers on Midjourney's own account/billing page before subscribing.

There's no dedicated store entry for Midjourney on this site yet, so there's no coupon page to link to here.

## Features that actually differentiate it

**Default aesthetic quality.** This is the single biggest reason people pick Midjourney over free or cheaper alternatives. Even a short, unrefined prompt tends to produce something usable — good lighting, coherent composition, a level of "finish" that other generators often need heavier prompt engineering to match.

**Style Reference and Character Reference.** You can feed Midjourney a reference image and weight to pull its aesthetic (`--sref`) or a consistent character/subject (`--cref`) into new generations. This is genuinely useful for producing a series — book illustrations, a brand's visual identity, a recurring mascot — that need to look consistent across dozens of separate prompts.

**Vary (Region) and inpainting.** Rather than regenerating a whole image because one element is wrong, you can select just a region — a face, a background object — and regenerate only that part while the rest stays fixed, closing a gap that used to force people into Photoshop for small fixes.

**Niji models for anime/illustration.** A meaningfully different aesthetic target from the base model, tuned specifically for anime and stylized illustration rather than trying to be a generalist model that also does anime passably.

**Editable web app.** The panning/zooming/region-edit toolkit in the web interface, rather than juggling Discord slash commands, makes iterating on a specific image far less painful than the original Discord-only workflow — the biggest usability upgrade the product has had since launch.

## Who it's actually for

- **Solo creators and hobbyists** experimenting with AI art casually will likely find the $10 Basic plan tight — 3.3 fast hours a month disappears quickly once you start iterating, so budget for either relax-mode queue times or stepping up to Standard.
- **Freelancers and small studios** producing client-facing visuals (concept art, book covers, marketing assets) are the core audience for Standard or Pro — Pro's stealth mode matters if you're working on unreleased client projects you don't want appearing in Midjourney's public feed.
- **Agencies and teams generating at volume** across multiple campaigns or product lines are the target for Mega, where 60 fast-hours and stealth mode justify $120/month against running several separate lower-tier accounts.
- **Anyone needing precise, deterministic output** (exact text rendering, exact logo placement, pixel-level control) should treat Midjourney as a starting point, not a finishing tool — it's a probabilistic generator, not a design program, and will need touch-up work in an actual editor.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- |
| Strong default image quality with minimal prompt effort | No permanent free tier — every account needs a paid plan to generate |
| Style/character reference tools genuinely help visual consistency across a series | Discord-based origin still shows; the web app is better but community-feed culture bleeds through |
| Web app removes most of the old Discord-only friction | Fast-hour allotments run out quickly once you're iterating heavily |
| Niji models give a real second aesthetic lane for anime/illustration work | Text rendering inside images, while improved, is still not fully reliable |
| Commercial usage rights included on all paid plans | Lower tiers publish your generations to a public feed unless you're on Pro/Mega |

## Integrations and ecosystem

Midjourney doesn't offer a first-party public API for developers to build on top of — access is through the Discord bot or the official web app only, a real limitation if you wanted to wire image generation into your own app or automation pipeline (Zapier-style integrations exist only informally, via third parties automating the Discord interface, which are unsupported and can violate the terms of service). There's no native Slack, Notion or design-tool plugin either. If you specifically need programmatic, API-first image generation for a product you're building, look at API-first competitors instead. What Midjourney does integrate well with is Discord itself, and, informally, any workflow where you're happy to download finished PNGs into whatever design tool you already use.

## Where it's a strong fit

Midjourney earns its subscription price for anyone doing repeated concept art, mood-boarding, stylized marketing visuals, or illustration work where "looks great by default" matters more than exact control. Teams producing a steady stream of visual content — blog headers, ad creative, character concepts — get real value out of the reference tools once they've learned the prompt syntax, and the web app's editing tools have closed most of the gap that used to send people to a separate editor for small fixes.

## Where to think twice

Skip Midjourney, or at least don't lead with it, if you need a genuinely free tool with no ongoing cost — there isn't one, and free trials are inconsistent and often unavailable. Skip it too if you need API access to build image generation into your own product, since Midjourney has no supported developer API. Teams with strict compliance or enterprise data-handling requirements should check Midjourney's terms directly rather than assume formal enterprise contracts exist, since its support structure is still built primarily around individual and small-team subscriptions. And if exact, literal output — precise text, exact brand colors, pixel-perfect layout — matters more than aesthetic quality, a probabilistic generator like this will frustrate you; budget time for manual touch-ups regardless of which plan you pick.

## Bottom line

Midjourney remains one of the strongest choices for AI image generation if what you're after is polished, aesthetically strong output without needing to fight the tool for it. It's not the cheapest option and has no meaningful free tier, but the combination of default output quality, the reference tools for consistency across a series, and a genuinely improved web editing interface make the Standard or Pro plan a reasonable recurring cost for anyone who generates images regularly. If your use case is occasional or you need API access, look elsewhere first.

[Try Midjourney](/go/offer/midjourney)

## Frequently asked questions

**Does Midjourney have a free plan?**
No ongoing free tier exists as of this writing — every account needs an active paid subscription (Basic and up) to generate images. Midjourney has occasionally offered limited free trials in the past and pulled them due to abuse, so don't assume one will be available when you sign up.

**What's the cheapest way to try Midjourney?**
The $10/month Basic plan (or its discounted annual equivalent) is the lowest-cost entry point. Given the limited fast-hours on Basic, expect to spend most of your time in the slower relax-mode queue unless you upgrade.

**Can I use Midjourney images commercially?**
Yes, all paid plans include commercial usage rights for images you generate, though Midjourney's terms of service have extra requirements for larger companies above a specific revenue threshold — read the current terms directly before using output for a larger commercial venture.

**Does Midjourney keep my generations private?**
Only Pro and Mega plans include stealth mode, which keeps your generations off Midjourney's public community feed. On Basic and Standard, your prompts and images are visible in the public feed by default.

**Is Midjourney better than other AI image generators?**
"Better" depends on the use case — Midjourney generally has an edge on default aesthetic polish, but other generators may edge it out on exact prompt adherence, price, or having a genuinely free tier. If you need programmatic API access, competitors that offer a developer API are the better fit regardless of image quality.

**Do I need to use Discord to use Midjourney?**
No — since mid-2024 Midjourney has offered its own web app with image generation and editing built in, now the more common way most subscribers work. Discord access is still available if you prefer the original workflow.

**Is Midjourney beginner-friendly?**
It's approachable to start (type a prompt, get an image) but has a real learning curve to get consistently strong results — style weight, aspect ratio flags and reference-image syntax take some practice. Budget an hour or two of experimentation before judging fit.

**How often does Midjourney release new models?**
Midjourney has released major version updates roughly every several months to a year historically (V4 through the V7/V8-series), each generally improving prompt adherence, coherence and text rendering — check Midjourney's own changelog for the exact current model version.

For more AI and software coverage, see the [AI & software deals](/category/software) category.

title: A2 Hosting Review 2026: Now Hosting.com — Verdict
excerpt: A2 Hosting was rebranded to Hosting.com in 2025 — here's what changed, what stayed the same, and whether it's still worth choosing.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## A2 Hosting Review 2026: What Happened to the Brand, and Is It Worth It?

A2 Hosting no longer exists as an independent brand — it was acquired by World Host Group in January 2025 and rebranded as hosting.com in April 2025. The infrastructure, cPanel-based shared hosting, and account systems carried over; the old Startup/Drive/Turbo Boost/Turbo Max plans were simply renamed Starter/Plus/Pro/Max, with NVMe storage now standard on every tier instead of just the premium ones.

### At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | $3.99/month (Starter, 1-year term) |
| Renewal price | Not published; independent reviews report a steep increase, commonly cited around $11-$28/month depending on tier |
| Uptime guarantee | 99.9% with service credits |
| Money-back guarantee | 30 days |
| Control panel | cPanel |
| Best for | Sites that want NVMe/LiteSpeed performance on an entry-level plan |

### What A2 Hosting actually is now

If you searched for "A2 Hosting" expecting to land on a2hosting.com, you'd have been redirected — the domain now forwards to hosting.com. World Host Group, which already owns several hosting brands, bought A2 Hosting in January 2025 and folded it into hosting.com a few months later as part of a broader consolidation. This isn't a shutdown: the shared hosting product, cPanel setup, and NVMe-backed infrastructure A2 was known for are still being sold, just under a new name and with a simplified four-tier lineup. Long-time A2 customers have reported a rockier transition period with support response times, though multiple 2026 reviews note that response times have recovered since.

For anyone comparing hosts today, this matters because pricing pages, coupon codes, and reviews still referencing "A2 Hosting Turbo" or "A2 Hosting Startup" are describing a product that has since been renamed and repriced — treat older A2-branded pricing screenshots as outdated.

### Pricing table

Pricing accurate as of September 2026 and subject to change — verify current rates at checkout.

| Plan (formerly) | Price | Storage | Websites |
|---|---|---|---|
| Starter (Startup) | $3.99/mo | 15GB NVMe | 1 |
| Plus (Drive) | $3.99/mo | 30GB NVMe | 2 |
| Pro (Turbo Boost) | $6.99/mo | 50GB NVMe | 10 |
| Max (Turbo Max) | $8.99/mo | 100GB NVMe | 100 |

All four tiers now include NVMe storage, LiteSpeed caching, unlimited bandwidth, unlimited databases, free SSL, and a free domain for the first year on annual terms — features that used to be split between A2's standard and Turbo lineups are now bundled into every plan.

### The real cost breakdown

The prices above are the introductory rate on a 1-year term, not what you'll pay indefinitely. hosting.com doesn't publish an exact renewal figure on its pricing page — a departure from A2's old habit of showing renewal pricing up front — but multiple independent reviews of the post-rebrand pricing report renewal invoices landing well above the intro rate, with figures cited in roughly the $11-$28/month range depending on the tier and term length chosen. Because the exact number isn't disclosed publicly, add the plan to your cart and check the renewal price hosting.com shows at checkout before you commit, rather than assuming the first-year price is permanent. The free first-year domain also reverts to a standard renewal price at the registrar rate once that year is up.

### Which plan should you choose

- **Choose Starter** if you're launching a single small site — a portfolio, a local business page, or a blog — and don't need room to grow beyond one domain.
- **Choose Plus** if you're running two small sites, or want a little more storage headroom than Starter without paying Pro pricing.
- **Choose Pro** if you're managing up to 10 sites, such as a freelancer or small agency hosting a handful of client sites on one account.
- **Choose Max** if you need capacity for many sites (up to 100) on a single plan — useful for a larger portfolio of low-traffic sites, though a single high-traffic site would outgrow shared hosting regardless of tier.

### Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| NVMe storage and LiteSpeed caching now included on every tier, not just premium ones | Exact renewal pricing isn't published — you have to check at checkout |
| cPanel, a control panel most site owners already know | Brand transition has caused confusion about which product you're actually buying |
| 30-day money-back guarantee | Some long-time A2 customers reported a dip in support quality right after the acquisition |
| Free domain and SSL on annual plans | Shared hosting still means shared server resources regardless of the rebrand |

### Support

hosting.com offers the support channels A2 customers were used to — live chat and a ticketing system are the primary channels for shared hosting customers. Reviews from 2026 indicate response times dipped during the immediate post-acquisition transition in 2025 but have since recovered; it's still worth checking current chat wait times before you buy if fast support response is a priority for you.

### Migration

Free website migration is included, continuing a feature A2 was known for. If you're moving from another cPanel-based host, migration tends to be the most straightforward, since hosting.com's shared plans run on the same control panel most budget hosts use — expect more manual work if you're migrating off a host with a custom, non-cPanel dashboard.

### Where it's a strong fit

- You want NVMe/LiteSpeed-class performance without paying for a premium "Turbo" tier — that's now the default across the board.
- You're comfortable with cPanel and want a familiar admin experience rather than a proprietary dashboard.
- You're consolidating several low-traffic sites onto one account and want the higher website-count ceiling the Pro or Max tiers offer.

### Where to think twice

- You want full pricing transparency before you commit — the lack of a published renewal rate means you have to dig for it at checkout.
- You specifically wanted to buy from "A2 Hosting" as a brand — that name no longer represents an independently operated company.
- You're deciding based on A2's older reputation for turbo-tier performance without checking that the product you'd actually be buying today is the renamed, restructured hosting.com lineup.

### Bottom line

The hosting product formerly sold as A2 Hosting is still a reasonable shared hosting option — NVMe storage and LiteSpeed caching across every tier is a genuine improvement over A2's old premium-only Turbo model, and the cPanel setup and 30-day guarantee carried over intact. The catch is the same one that dogs most budget hosts: the eye-catching intro price isn't the real long-term cost, and here it's compounded by hosting.com not publishing the renewal rate outright. If you go in expecting to check the renewal figure at checkout and budget for a multi-year cost rather than the first invoice, it's a solid pick for small-to-mid site counts on a familiar control panel.

### FAQs

**Is A2 Hosting still around?**
Not as an independent company. A2 Hosting was acquired by World Host Group in January 2025 and rebranded as hosting.com in April 2025. The a2hosting.com domain now redirects to hosting.com.

**What are A2's old plans called now?**
Startup became Starter, Drive became Plus, Turbo Boost became Pro, and Turbo Max became Max.

**What does hosting.com's shared hosting cost?**
Starter and Plus both start at $3.99/month, Pro at $6.99/month, and Max at $8.99/month, on a 1-year introductory term. Renewal pricing is higher but isn't published on the pricing page — confirm it at checkout.

**Does hosting.com use cPanel?**
Yes, shared hosting runs on the standard cPanel control panel, the same as it did under A2.

**Is there a free domain and SSL?**
A free domain is included for the first year on annual plans, and SSL certificates are free on all shared hosting plans.

**What's the money-back guarantee?**
30 days on new shared hosting purchases. It doesn't cover domain registrations/renewals or certain add-on services.

**Is migration free?**
Yes, free website migration is included, a feature that carried over from A2.

**Did support get worse after the A2-to-hosting.com transition?**
Some long-time A2 customers reported slower support response right after the January 2025 acquisition, but multiple 2026 reviews note response times have recovered since.

Compare current offers on the [A2 Hosting coupon page](/coupons/a2hosting), or browse more [Web hosting deals](/category/hosting).

title: Bluehost Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: Bluehost's real Starter-to-eCommerce pricing, renewal costs, cPanel setup, migration and support — an evidence-based look at whether it's worth it.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Bluehost a good hosting choice in 2026?

Bluehost is a solid pick for beginners who want cPanel, an official WordPress recommendation, and a free domain — but its lowest prices require a 36-month prepay and more than double at renewal. It's a reasonable default for a first website, less competitive if you plan to keep costs flat past year one.

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | $3.99/month (Starter, 36-month term) |
| Renewal price | $9.99/month (Starter) |
| Control panel | cPanel |
| Uptime guarantee | 99.99% SLA |
| Money-back guarantee | 30 days |
| Best for | Beginners and small WordPress sites wanting cPanel |

## What Bluehost actually is

Bluehost is one of the longest-running mainstream web hosts, owned by Newfold Digital, and has been an officially recommended host on WordPress.org for years. It runs shared, WordPress-specific, VPS, dedicated and a newer cloud hosting line. The shared and WordPress plans use cPanel, the industry-standard control panel most hosting guides and tutorials are written for — a practical advantage if you'll ever need help from a non-Bluehost-specific source or want to move providers later, since cPanel accounts are broadly portable.

## Pricing

Bluehost's shared hosting comes in three tiers. These are the introductory rates on the cheapest available term (36 months), current as of this post's publish date — hosting prices change periodically, so confirm the live rate on Bluehost's pricing page before buying.

| Plan | Intro price/mo | Renewal price/mo | Storage | Websites |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Starter | $3.99 | $9.99 | 10GB NVMe | 10 |
| Business | $6.99 | $13.99 | 50GB NVMe | 50 |
| eCommerce Essentials | $14.99 | $21.99 | 100GB NVMe | 100 |

All three include a free domain for the first year, a free SSL certificate, and a 99.99% uptime SLA. Business and eCommerce Essentials add a free CDN.

## The real cost breakdown

The advertised $3.99/month Starter price only applies if you prepay the full 36-month term up front — that's roughly $144 charged at checkout, not $3.99. Pay monthly or choose a shorter term instead, and the rate is meaningfully higher from day one.

More importantly, none of these are the price you keep paying. Once the initial term ends, Starter renews at $9.99/month, Business at $13.99/month, and eCommerce Essentials at $21.99/month — each roughly 1.5x to 2.5x the intro rate. The free first-year domain also reverts to Bluehost's standard domain renewal price in year two. None of this is hidden exactly, but it's easy to overlook when the homepage banner only shows the small number. Budget for the renewal price, not the promotional one, when deciding whether Bluehost fits your budget long-term.

## Which plan should you choose

**Choose Starter** if you're launching one small site — a blog, portfolio, or single-business page — and don't need more than 10GB of storage or multiple domains.

**Choose Business** if you're running several sites under one account, want a CDN included, or expect enough traffic that 50GB of storage and higher resource limits matter.

**Choose eCommerce Essentials** if you're building a store — it adds ecommerce-specific tooling on top of the Business plan's resources, though for a serious storefront it's worth comparing against dedicated ecommerce hosting or platforms before committing.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Uses standard cPanel, not a proprietary dashboard | Lowest price requires a 36-month prepay |
| Free domain and SSL included in year one | Renewal prices are 1.5-2.5x the intro rate |
| Official WordPress.org recommended host | Free domain reverts to standard pricing after year one |
| 99.99% uptime SLA and 24/7 chat support | Cloud hosting tier drops cPanel entirely |

## Support

Bluehost offers 24/7 live chat and phone support across its shared hosting plans, plus a large self-serve knowledge base covering cPanel, WordPress, domains, SSL and DNS. Trustpilot feedback is mixed on support wait times and consistency between agents, though most recent reviews describe support as responsive and able to resolve issues in one interaction.

## Migration

Bluehost provides a website migration process for moving an existing site onto its hosting, including WordPress-specific migration tools. As with most hosts, free migrations are typically limited in scope (e.g. a single site) — check current terms before assuming a complex multi-site migration is included at no cost, and back up your existing site independently before starting any transfer.

## Where it's a strong fit

- First website or blog where cPanel familiarity and WordPress-specific guidance matter more than rock-bottom long-term pricing.
- Sites likely to need standard hosting features (email, staging, SSH) without paying for a higher-tier plan.
- Buyers comfortable prepaying multiple years to lock in the lowest rate and who won't be caught off guard by the renewal jump.

## Where to think twice

- If you want a flat, predictable monthly cost from month one, since Bluehost's advertised price is explicitly a limited-time new-customer rate.
- If you specifically want to avoid a long upfront commitment — the cheapest per-month rate is tied to the 36-month term, not to monthly billing.
- If you're set on Bluehost Cloud hosting and want cPanel — that product line doesn't include it.

## Bottom line

Bluehost remains a reasonable, well-established choice for a first website, mainly on the strength of cPanel, WordPress's own recommendation, and broad support coverage. The catch isn't hidden, but it is easy to skim past: the headline price is a 36-month-prepay, new-customer rate that renews at up to 2.5x higher. Go in planning around the renewal price, not the banner price, and Bluehost is a solid, unremarkable-in-a-good-way host. Go in expecting the intro price to hold, and renewal will feel like a bait-and-switch.

Check current deals on the [Bluehost coupon page](/coupons/bluehost), or compare it against other providers on our [Web hosting deals](/category/hosting) page.

## FAQs

**Is Bluehost good for beginners?**
Yes — cPanel, one-click WordPress installs, and 24/7 chat support make it approachable for a first website, though the plan and pricing structure still rewards reading the fine print before buying.

**Does Bluehost use cPanel?**
Yes, on its shared, WordPress and VPS plans. Bluehost Cloud hosting is the exception and doesn't include cPanel.

**What does Bluehost cost after the first term?**
Shared hosting renews at $9.99/month (Starter), $13.99/month (Business) or $21.99/month (eCommerce Essentials) — noticeably more than the introductory rate, which only applies to the first term.

**Does Bluehost offer a free domain?**
Yes, a free domain registration for the first year on new hosting plans. It renews at Bluehost's standard domain pricing afterward.

**What is Bluehost's money-back guarantee?**
A 30-day money-back guarantee on hosting plans, letting you cancel within that window for a refund if it's not a fit.

**How does Bluehost handle site migrations?**
Bluehost offers migration support and WordPress-specific migration tools for moving an existing site over; free migrations are typically limited in scope, so confirm what's covered before a complex multi-site move.

**Is Bluehost better than Hostinger or Namecheap?**
It depends on priorities: Bluehost offers standard cPanel and WordPress.org's official recommendation, Hostinger uses its own simplified hPanel at a lower entry price, and Namecheap also runs cPanel with a longer-standing 30-day guarantee. Compare the specific renewal prices and storage limits for your use case rather than picking on brand alone.

**Can I pay monthly instead of prepaying years upfront?**
Bluehost's lowest advertised rate is tied to its longest (36-month) term. Monthly or shorter-term billing is typically available but at a higher effective rate — check the live pricing page for current monthly options.

title: ChemiCloud Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: ChemiCloud offers cPanel shared hosting on NVMe storage with a 45-day guarantee — here's what the plans cost and where renewal pricing catches buyers.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## ChemiCloud Review 2026: Is It Worth It?

ChemiCloud is a solid pick if you want standard cPanel hosting on NVMe storage with above-average support and a longer refund window. Its 45-day money-back guarantee beats the industry-standard 30 days, but like most budget hosts, its rock-bottom intro price jumps sharply at renewal — plan around that before you sign up for a long term.

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | $1.95/month (Starter, longest term) |
| Renewal price | $11.95-$21.95/month depending on plan |
| Control panel | cPanel |
| Money-back guarantee | 45 days (shared/WordPress/reseller); 7 days on VPS |
| Free domain | First year, requires a 36-month term |
| Best for | Small business and personal sites wanting cPanel + long refund window |

## What ChemiCloud actually is

ChemiCloud is a shared hosting company built around standard cPanel rather than a custom-built dashboard, which matters if you've used cPanel before or plan to migrate a site that already runs on it. Plans run on NVMe storage, use LiteSpeed Cache and a free Cloudflare CDN for performance, and include Imunify360 malware protection plus CloudLinux account isolation on the security side. Every tier also includes free daily backups, which some competitors reserve for higher-priced plans or charge extra for.

## Pricing table

Pricing below reflects ChemiCloud's own site as of this post's publish date (September 2026) and can change — always check the live pricing page before buying.

| Plan | Intro price | Renewal price | Websites | Storage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Starter | $1.95/mo | $11.95/mo | 1 | 20GB NVMe |
| Pro | $2.95/mo | $17.95/mo | Unlimited | 35GB NVMe |
| Turbo | $3.95/mo | $21.95/mo | Unlimited | 50GB NVMe |

## The real cost breakdown

The advertised prices above are introductory rates tied to the longest available billing term, applied only to that first term. Once it ends, every plan renews at the regular rate — $11.95/month for Starter, $17.95/month for Pro, and $21.95/month for Turbo. That's roughly a 5-6x jump from the sign-up price, which is steep even by shared-hosting standards, though the dollar renewal amounts themselves are in line with what Bluehost or Hostinger charge for comparable tiers.

There's a second catch worth knowing before checkout: the free first-year domain is only included if you commit to a 36-month term. Sign up for a shorter period and you'll either pay for your own domain or lose that perk. If you're not ready to commit for three years, factor the domain cost into your comparison against other hosts.

## Which plan should you choose

- **Choose Starter** if you're launching a single small site — a portfolio, a local business page, or a blog — and don't need more than 20GB of storage.
- **Choose Pro** if you're running more than one website, since it's the cheapest tier with unlimited websites and gives you extra storage headroom over Starter.
- **Choose Turbo** if you're running several higher-traffic sites or want the largest storage allowance before stepping up to VPS hosting.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| 45-day money-back guarantee, longer than most competitors | Renewal prices are 5-6x the intro rate |
| Standard cPanel, not a proprietary dashboard | Free domain requires a 36-month commitment |
| Free daily backups included on every plan | Storage caps are modest compared to some "unlimited storage" rivals |
| NVMe storage and free Cloudflare CDN on all tiers | Only 1 website allowed on the entry-level Starter plan |

## Support

ChemiCloud is frequently praised in customer reviews for responsive live chat and ticket support, which shows up in its strong Trustpilot rating. If support quality and quick response times matter more to you than saving another dollar a month, that reputation is one of ChemiCloud's stronger selling points relative to budget hosts that route more support through slower ticket queues.

## Migration

Because ChemiCloud runs standard cPanel, moving an existing cPanel-hosted site over is generally straightforward — most migrations can use cPanel-to-cPanel transfer tools or a plugin-based migration if you're on WordPress. Check ChemiCloud's own knowledge base for current migration assistance options before you cancel service with your old host, since free migration availability and scope can vary by plan.

## Where it's a strong fit

ChemiCloud makes sense if you want familiar cPanel hosting, plan to test the service risk-free thanks to the 45-day window, and are running one to a handful of small-to-medium sites that fit comfortably within the storage tiers above.

## Where to think twice

## Bottom line

Compare the renewal price, not just the sign-up price, before committing.

45 days on shared, WordPress and reseller hosting — longer than the 30-day standard at most competitors. VPS hosting only gets a 7-day window.

Just one on the Starter plan. Pro and Turbo both allow unlimited websites.

title: DreamHost Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: DreamHost review covering shared hosting plans, real renewal pricing, its custom control panel, migration tools, support and who it fits best.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## DreamHost Review 2026: Is It Worth the Renewal Price?

DreamHost is a solid budget host for beginners and small sites, built on a custom control panel instead of cPanel, with a genuine 30-day money-back guarantee. Its entry Launch plan starts at $2.89/month but renews at $10.99/month — a real jump you should plan for before signing up on a long term.

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | $2.89/month (Launch, first year) |
| Renewal price | $10.99/month (Launch) |
| Control panel | Custom DreamHost panel (no cPanel) |
| Uptime | No general uptime guarantee widely advertised on plan pages |
| Money-back guarantee | 30 days (credit card purchases; domain fees non-refundable) |
| Best for | Beginners and small sites wanting predictable, unmetered shared hosting |

## What DreamHost actually is

DreamHost is a web hosting company that's been operating since 1996, offering shared hosting, WordPress-optimized hosting (DreamPress), VPS, and dedicated servers. Unlike most budget hosts that license cPanel, DreamHost built its own control panel from scratch. It handles domains, email, databases, one-click installs and SSL from a single dashboard, but the interface and terminology differ from cPanel, so anyone migrating from a cPanel host will need a short adjustment period rather than a drop-in replacement.

DreamHost also positions itself around data privacy commitments (it publicly opposed government data requests in the past) and offers a free tier of WordPress hosting for qualifying nonprofits — a niche but genuine differentiator most budget hosts don't offer.

## Pricing table

| Plan | Websites | Storage | Intro price | Renewal price |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Launch | 25 | 25GB NVMe SSD | $2.89/mo | $10.99/mo |
| Growth | 50 | 50GB NVMe SSD | $3.99/mo | $12.99/mo |
| Scale | 100 | 100GB NVMe SSD | $9.99/mo | $25.99/mo |

Pricing was accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — check DreamHost's current pricing page before buying.

## The real cost breakdown

The advertised price is what you pay for the first year only, generally requiring at least an annual commitment upfront. After that first term, the plan renews at the standard rate — for the entry Launch plan, that's a jump from $2.89/month to $10.99/month, close to 4x the intro rate. Growth goes from $3.99 to $12.99/month, and Scale from $9.99 to $25.99/month.

All three tiers include a free domain for the first year and unlimited free SSL certificates, which offsets some of the first-year cost. DreamHost also throws in a professional email trial for three months; if you keep using it past that window, it's billed as a separate add-on, so budget for that if your workflow depends on branded email. Domain registration fees themselves are not covered by the money-back guarantee even if you cancel hosting.

## Which plan should you choose

- **Choose Launch** if you're running one to a handful of small sites (blogs, portfolios, local business sites) and don't need more than 25GB of storage — it's the cheapest entry point and covers most first-website use cases.
- **Choose Growth** if you're managing several sites (an agency with a handful of client sites, or a personal site plus a couple of side projects) and want double the storage and website allowance without jumping to VPS.
- **Choose Scale** if you're running many sites off one account, need the largest inode allowance DreamHost offers on shared hosting, or expect meaningfully more disk usage than the lower tiers allow — but at this price point it's worth comparing against a small VPS plan for the same money.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Genuine unmetered bandwidth on every tier | Custom panel means no cPanel compatibility with existing workflows |
| Free domain + free SSL included in year one | Renewal pricing is 3-4x the intro rate |
| High Trustpilot rating (4.6/5 from over 8,000 reviews) | No 24/7 phone support — chat and tickets only |
| Free automated WordPress migration plugin | Free professional email is only a 3-month trial, then billed separately |

## Support

DreamHost offers 24/7 live chat in English and Spanish, plus a ticket-based support system and an extensive self-serve knowledge base. There's no inbound phone support line for general technical issues — DreamHost instead offers scheduled callbacks, which are prioritized in the support queue but not a substitute for calling in directly. If phone access matters to you, weigh that against hosts that do offer it.

## Migration

DreamHost provides a free WordPress Automated Migration plugin, built with BlogVault, that moves site content, themes, plugins and configuration to DreamHost — DreamHost's own documentation says most migrations finish in under an hour, though larger or more complex sites can take longer. The plugin doesn't work with sites built on WordPress.com, Wix, Weebly, Squarespace or Joomla; those need a manual migration or DreamHost's paid professional migration service instead. For non-WordPress sites, migration is largely manual (file transfer plus database export/import through the DreamHost panel).

## Where it's a strong fit

DreamHost fits well for beginners launching their first one or two sites who want a straightforward, unmetered shared plan without needing to relearn cPanel from scratch. It's also a reasonable pick if a longer refund window at signup and genuinely unmetered bandwidth (rather than "unlimited" fine print) matter more to you than the absolute lowest renewal price. The nonprofit hosting option is worth a look for qualifying organizations.

## Where to think twice

If you're coming from a cPanel host and depend on cPanel-specific plugins or a familiar workflow, DreamHost's custom panel is a genuine switching cost, not just a cosmetic difference. Anyone who needs phone support for troubleshooting should also look elsewhere, since DreamHost keeps support to chat and tickets. And if you plan to keep a site on the entry plan for years rather than upgrading, run the renewal math first — $10.99/month for Launch is no longer clearly cheaper than mid-tier competitors' every-year pricing.

## Bottom line

DreamHost is a credible, long-established budget host with real strengths — unmetered bandwidth, a free first-year domain, a strong Trustpilot track record, and a genuinely useful free WordPress migration tool. The custom control panel and the renewal-price jump are the two things to go in with eyes open about: it's not a drop-in cPanel replacement, and the price you sign up at is not the price you'll pay in year two. For a first site or a small handful of low-traffic sites, it's a reasonable choice as long as you plan for the renewal cost rather than being surprised by it.

## FAQs

**Is DreamHost good for beginners?**
Yes, for the most part — the custom panel is designed to be approachable, and setup for a first WordPress site is straightforward. The main adjustment is that it isn't cPanel, so tutorials written for cPanel hosts won't map one-to-one.

**Does DreamHost use cPanel?**
No. DreamHost built its own custom control panel rather than licensing cPanel, which is why it looks and behaves differently from most budget hosting competitors.

**What does DreamHost's shared hosting renew at?**
Launch renews at $10.99/month, Growth at $12.99/month, and Scale at $25.99/month, after the discounted first-year term ends.

**Does DreamHost offer a free domain?**
Yes, a free domain is included for the first year on its Web Hosting plans.

**How long is DreamHost's money-back guarantee?**
30 days on shared hosting plans paid by credit card, per DreamHost's current pricing page; domain registration fees are excluded from any refund.

**Can DreamHost migrate my WordPress site for free?**
Yes, via its free Automated Migration plugin, which DreamHost says typically completes in under an hour for most WordPress sites. It doesn't support site builders like Wix or Squarespace.

**Does DreamHost have 24/7 support?**
Live chat is available 24/7 in English and Spanish. There is no general inbound phone support line; DreamHost offers scheduled callbacks instead.

**Is DreamHost cheaper than Hostinger or Namecheap?**
DreamHost's intro pricing is competitive with both, but all three follow the same pattern of a low first-term price that renews significantly higher — compare the renewal rate for the specific plan you'd actually keep, not just the advertised starting price. See our [Web hosting deals](/category/hosting) hub to compare current offers, or the [DreamHost coupon page](/coupons/dreamhost) for active discounts.

title: FastComet Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict

## Is FastComet a good web host in 2026?

FastComet is a solid pick if you want standard cPanel hosting on NVMe storage with a 30-day money-back guarantee and a 4.7-star Trustpilot rating from nearly 4,000 reviews. It's not the cheapest long-term, since renewal prices run 4-5x the intro rate, and the two lowest tiers cap you at one website.

| Best for | Beginners and small business sites wanting cPanel familiarity |

## What FastComet actually is

FastComet is a web hosting company offering shared, WordPress-optimized, cloud VPS and dedicated hosting, built entirely on standard cPanel rather than a proprietary dashboard. That's a meaningful difference from budget hosts like Hostinger, which built their own control panel — if you've used cPanel before, or you rely on migration tools and plugins that expect it, FastComet's setup will feel familiar immediately. The company also markets its shared plans as "WordPress hosting" with LiteSpeed caching, the WordPress Toolkit for mass updates, and a malware scanner bundled in.

## Pricing

FastComet sells four shared hosting tiers. Pricing below reflects the introductory term as of this post's publish date (September 2026) — hosting prices change often, so check FastComet's own pricing page for the current live offer before buying.

| Plan | Intro price | Storage | Websites |

| Essential | $2.99/mo | 20GB NVMe | 1 |
| Plus | $3.99/mo | 30GB NVMe | Unlimited |
| Extra | $5.49/mo | 40GB NVMe | Unlimited |

All four tiers include a free domain for the first term, free SSL, a Cloudflare CDN, and cPanel access.

## The real cost: intro vs. renewal

The advertised prices above only apply to the first billing term. After that, FastComet renews at a noticeably higher rate:

| Plan | Intro price | Renewal price |
|---|---|---|
| Starter | $1.99/mo | $9.95/mo |
| Essential | $2.99/mo | $12.95/mo |
| Plus | $3.99/mo | $17.95/mo |
| Extra | $5.49/mo | $24.95/mo |

That's roughly a 4-5x increase once the promotional term ends, which is a bigger jump than some competitors and worth factoring into a multi-year cost comparison rather than judging FastComet on the headline price alone. There's also a structural catch that's easy to miss: the Starter and Essential plans are capped at one website each, so if you're planning even a second small site, you need Plus or higher regardless of what the entry-level price advertises.

## Which plan should you choose

- **Choose Starter** if you're launching exactly one small site (a portfolio, a landing page, a simple blog) and don't expect to add a second domain later.
- **Choose Essential** if you want more storage headroom for that single site — more images, a bigger media library — but still only need one website.
- **Choose Plus** if you're running, or plan to run, more than one website; the jump to unlimited sites at this tier is the main reason to skip past Essential.
- **Choose Extra** if you're managing several higher-traffic sites and want the most storage and performance headroom FastComet's shared tier offers before stepping up to cloud VPS.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Standard cPanel, not a proprietary dashboard | Renewal prices are 4-5x the intro rate |
| NVMe SSD storage on every shared tier | Starter and Essential cap out at 1 website |
| 4.7-star Trustpilot rating across ~3,900 reviews | Intro pricing requires committing to a term to get the advertised rate |
| Free domain, SSL and CDN included | Storage limits (10-40GB) are modest next to some "unlimited storage" competitors |
| 30-day money-back guarantee | |

## Support

FastComet advertises 24/7 support and is generally well-reviewed for response times on Trustpilot, where the bulk of its ~3,900 reviews are 5-star. As with any host, the depth of support matters more once you're past basic setup questions and into things like DNS troubleshooting or performance tuning — check current live-chat/ticket response times before committing if that's a priority, since support quality can shift over time even when the marketing page doesn't change.

## Migration

FastComet is built on cPanel, which is the main practical advantage for migration: most existing cPanel hosting accounts can move over using standard cPanel-to-cPanel transfer tools rather than a proprietary import process. If you're coming from a host that uses its own custom panel (Hostinger's hPanel, for example), expect a more manual migration since there's no like-for-like automated path between different panel systems.

## Where it's a strong fit

FastComet works well if you specifically want cPanel (not a custom dashboard), you're comfortable with the idea that the price you pay today isn't the price you'll pay long-term, and you're starting with one or two sites rather than a large portfolio. The free domain, free SSL and NVMe storage on even the cheapest tier make it a reasonable entry point for a first website.

## Where to think twice

If you're planning several websites from day one, skip Starter and Essential and budget for Plus or Extra — otherwise you'll hit the one-site cap quickly. And if the multi-year cost matters more to you than the sign-up price, compare FastComet's renewal rates directly against competitors' renewal rates, not their intro rates, before deciding.

## Bottom line

FastComet is a reasonable choice for anyone who wants standard cPanel hosting with NVMe storage and doesn't mind that the advertised price is a first-term promotion rather than what they'll pay ongoing. Its Trustpilot record is genuinely strong, and the cPanel foundation makes it easy to migrate in or out later. The two things to plan around are the roughly 4-5x renewal jump and the one-website ceiling on the two cheapest tiers — budget for the plan you'll actually need, not just the cheapest sign-up price.

## FAQs

**Does FastComet use cPanel?**
Yes, all shared, WordPress, cloud VPS and dedicated hosting plans run on standard cPanel.

**What is FastComet's money-back guarantee?**
FastComet offers a 30-day money-back guarantee on its hosting plans.

**Does FastComet's advertised price stay the same after renewal?**
No. Introductory pricing applies to the first term only; renewal rates run $9.95-$24.95/month depending on plan, roughly 4-5x the intro price.

**Can I host multiple websites on FastComet's cheapest plan?**
No — the Starter and Essential plans are limited to one website each. Unlimited websites require the Plus plan or higher.

**Does FastComet include a free domain?**
Yes, all four shared hosting tiers include a free domain for the first term.

**How much storage do FastComet's shared plans include?**
Storage runs from 10GB NVMe SSD on Starter up to 40GB NVMe SSD on Extra, scaling with each tier.

**Is FastComet good for beginners?**
Its use of standard cPanel (rather than a custom panel) means beginners who've seen cPanel tutorials elsewhere will find plenty of familiar documentation, and the free SSL/CDN/domain bundle removes some early setup decisions.

**What do FastComet reviews say?**
FastComet holds a 4.7 out of 5 rating on Trustpilot from around 3,900 reviews, with the large majority being 5-star.

## What GoDaddy actually is

GoDaddy is the world's largest domain registrar by volume, and web hosting is one of several products it sells alongside domains, a website builder, business email and marketing tools. GoDaddy provides guided site-migration help for moving an existing site onto its hosting, and because it runs standard cPanel, a cPanel-to-cPanel migration from another host is generally straightforward using cPanel's own backup/restore tools or GoDaddy's migration service. ## Where it's a strong fit

- You value phone support as an option alongside chat.
- You're hosting a moderate number of client or personal sites and Deluxe/Ultimate's site limits fit your needs.

## Where to think twice

## Bottom line

GoDaddy backs its web hosting plans with a 30-day money-back guarantee.

Economy allows 1 website, Deluxe allows up to 10, and Ultimate allows up to 25 — all on the same shared hosting account.

title: GreenGeeks Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: GreenGeeks pairs renewable-energy-matched cPanel hosting with free nightly backups. Here's what it costs, what's included, and who it fits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is GreenGeeks a good hosting choice?

GreenGeeks is a solid pick if you want standard cPanel hosting with free nightly backups and a genuine environmental angle — it purchases renewable energy credits equal to 300% of its power draw. It's not the cheapest option once renewal pricing kicks in, and its intro-to-renewal jump is one of the steeper ones in budget shared hosting.

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | $2.95/month (Lite plan, intro term) |
| Renewal price | $13.95/month (Lite), up to $30.95/month (Premium) |
| Money-back guarantee | 30 days |
| Control panel | cPanel |
| Free domain | Yes, first year on annual+ terms |
| Best for | Beginners and small sites wanting cPanel + eco-conscious hosting |

## What GreenGeeks actually is

GreenGeeks is a privately held web host founded in 2008, built around shared, WordPress, VPS and reseller hosting on standard cPanel — not a custom-built dashboard like some budget competitors use. Its main differentiator is sustainability marketing: GreenGeeks says it buys renewable energy credits through the Bonneville Environmental Foundation equal to 300% of the power its infrastructure consumes from the grid, and it has partnered with One Tree Planted on reforestation efforts. The servers themselves still run on ordinary grid electricity in commercial data centers — the "green" claim is about offsetting via purchased credits, not off-grid or on-site renewable power.

Beyond the sustainability angle, the hosting stack itself is fairly conventional for the price tier: LiteSpeed web servers, HTTP/3 support, Redis object caching, and a 1-click installer covering 150+ applications including WordPress.

## Pricing

| Plan | Intro price | Websites | Storage | Notable extras |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lite | $2.95/mo | 1 | 25GB SSD | Unmetered bandwidth, free SSL |
| Pro | $4.95/mo | Unlimited | 50GB SSD | Free CDN, nightly backups |
| Premium | $8.95/mo | Unlimited | 100GB SSD | Dedicated IP, priority support |

All three tiers include cPanel, a free domain for the first year on annual or longer billing, free Let's Encrypt SSL, a free CDN, and free nightly backups.

## The real cost breakdown

The advertised $2.95-$8.95/month prices only apply to the initial signup term (typically billed upfront for 12, 24 or 36 months, longer terms unlocking the lowest per-month rate) and only to new accounts. Once that term ends, plans renew at:

- Lite: $13.95/month — roughly a 3.7x increase
- Pro: $18.95/month — roughly a 3.8x increase
- Premium: $30.95/month — roughly a 3.5x increase

That's a steeper intro-to-renewal ratio than several budget competitors, so the total cost over two or three years matters more than the sticker price on the landing page. If you register a free domain in year one, expect to pay standard domain renewal pricing from year two onward as well.

## Which plan should you choose

- **Choose Lite** if you're launching a single small site — a blog, portfolio or brochure site — and don't need room to grow to multiple domains.
- **Choose Pro** if you run more than one website, or expect to add sites later; the jump to unlimited websites and double the storage for roughly $2/month more (at intro pricing) makes it the more practical default for most buyers.
- **Choose Premium** if you need a dedicated IP address (for a standalone SSL certificate outside shared hosting norms, or specific compliance requirements) or you're hosting resource-heavier sites that benefit from the extra storage headroom.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Standard cPanel, not a proprietary dashboard | Renewal prices roughly 3.5-4x the intro rate |
| Free nightly backups included on shared plans | Lite plan caps you at one website |
| Renewable-energy-credit purchases (300% match) | "Green" claim is credit-based offsetting, not on-site renewable power |
| Free CDN and Let's Encrypt SSL on every plan | Dedicated IP reserved for the top Premium tier |

## Support

GreenGeeks offers 24/7 support through live chat, phone and a ticketing system, backed by a knowledge base covering common cPanel and WordPress tasks. Premium-tier customers get priority placement in support queues, but chat and phone access aren't gated behind a specific plan.

## Migration

GreenGeeks provides free website migration for new customers moving from another host, typically handled by its in-house migration team rather than a self-service plugin-only process. This covers standard cPanel-to-cPanel site transfers; more complex custom setups may need to be scoped with support first.

## Where it's a strong fit

GreenGeeks makes sense if you specifically want cPanel (rather than a custom panel) at a budget-hosting price point, you value free nightly backups without paying extra for them, or the renewable-energy-credit angle is a genuine factor in your purchasing decision. It's also a reasonable fit for small agencies managing a handful of client sites on the Pro tier.

## Where to think twice

If you're price-sensitive over a multi-year horizon, the renewal jump is worth running the numbers on before committing to a long initial term — a competitor with a smaller intro-to-renewal gap could cost less by year three even with a slightly higher headline price today. Buyers who specifically want a simplified, non-cPanel dashboard should also look elsewhere.

## Bottom line

GreenGeeks is a competent, cPanel-based shared host with a genuinely differentiated environmental pitch and useful included extras like nightly backups and a free CDN. The tradeoff is a renewal price that climbs well above the introductory rate, so it earns a recommendation for buyers who've budgeted for that step-up rather than those chasing the lowest possible long-term cost.

## Where it's a strong fit

## Where it's a strong fit

- You want NVMe-speed storage without paying for a premium managed host.
- You're comfortable learning a new (if simpler) dashboard instead of cPanel.
- You're launching a new site rather than migrating a complex existing one.
- You want a free domain bundled into your first year of hosting.

## Where to think twice

- You depend on cPanel-specific tools (Softaculous, cron job UI, detailed cPanel logs) for your workflow.
- You're migrating a large, complex site and want a same-panel, low-friction transfer.
- You want the lowest possible price to hold steady past year one — budget for the renewal jump.

## Bottom line

IONOS is a reasonable choice for beginners and small sites that want fast NVMe storage, a free domain, and a straightforward (if unfamiliar) dashboard at a low entry price. It's not the pick for anyone who wants cPanel compatibility or expects the intro price to hold past the first term — factor the renewal rate into your decision before committing to a multi-year plan.

## FAQs

**Does IONOS offer a free trial?**
IONOS doesn't advertise a free trial for shared hosting, but it does back plans with a 30-day money-back guarantee, which functions similarly if you decide it's not the right fit early on.

**Can I use WordPress with IONOS?**
Yes. IONOS supports one-click WordPress installation on its shared hosting plans, and the Ultimate tier's higher PHP memory limit is specifically useful for larger WordPress or WooCommerce installs.

**Does IONOS have a cPanel option?**
No. All shared hosting plans use IONOS's own "My IONOS" control panel. There's no way to add cPanel to a shared plan.

**What happens to my price after the first year?**
Your plan renews at IONOS's standard rate for that tier — noticeably higher than the intro price, roughly double on the lower tiers. Check your specific renewal notice, since IONOS adjusted some renewal pricing in 2026.

**Is IONOS good for beginners?**
It can be — the My IONOS panel is generally considered simpler to navigate than cPanel for basic tasks like email setup and one-click installs, though it has fewer advanced options for power users.

**Does IONOS include email hosting?**
Yes, each shared hosting plan includes a set number of professional email accounts (from 1 on Essential up to 5 on Ultimate), tied to your domain.

**How does IONOS handle backups?**
IONOS includes backup functionality through the My IONOS dashboard, though the specifics (frequency, retention) vary by plan — check your plan's details before relying on it as your only backup.

**Is there a contract or can I pay monthly?**
IONOS's lowest advertised prices require signing up for a longer upfront term (commonly 12 months, billed at signup); shorter or month-to-month billing is typically available but at a higher effective rate.

title: ScalaHosting Review 2026: Pricing and Verdict

body:
## Is ScalaHosting a good hosting provider?

ScalaHosting is a solid pick if you want managed cloud VPS performance without cPanel licensing fees, thanks to its free in-house SPanel control panel. Its cheap shared hosting is fine for a small first site, but the standard 3-4x renewal jump means it isn't the cheapest long-term option — read the fine print before committing to a multi-year term.

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | $2.95/month (Mini shared hosting) |
| Renewal price | $11.95/month (Mini) |
| Control panel | cPanel (shared) / SPanel (cloud VPS) |
| Money-back guarantee | 30 days (new customers, hosting only) |
| Best for | Sites that want to grow into managed cloud VPS later |

## What ScalaHosting actually is

ScalaHosting is a hosting company built around two product lines: standard cPanel-based shared hosting for small sites, and managed cloud VPS hosting that runs on SPanel — ScalaHosting's own free control panel, developed as an alternative to cPanel's per-account licensing costs. The company positions the VPS/cloud tier as its main product, with shared hosting acting as an entry point for smaller budgets.

That two-panel setup matters more than it might first look. On shared hosting you get the cPanel interface most hosting customers already know. Step up to cloud VPS and the panel changes to SPanel, which ScalaHosting controls entirely — meaning it can add features (like its SShield security layer) without waiting on a third-party cPanel release cycle, but also means anyone who's cPanel-only by habit has a small learning curve on the VPS side.

## Shared hosting pricing

Pricing was accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — check ScalaHosting's current pricing page before buying.

| Plan | Intro price | Websites | Storage | Control panel |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mini | $2.95/mo | 1 | 10GB NVMe | cPanel |
| Start | $5.95/mo | Unlimited | 50GB | cPanel |
| Advanced | $9.95/mo | Unlimited | 100GB | cPanel |

All three tiers include free SSL, unmetered bandwidth and free daily backups. Start and Advanced add a free domain for the first year.

## The real cost: intro vs. renewal

The advertised prices above are introductory rates tied to a longer upfront term. After that term ends, shared hosting renews at $11.95/month (Mini), $14.95/month (Start) and $19.95/month (Advanced) — roughly 3-4 times the sign-up price. That's a steeper renewal multiplier than some budget competitors, so it's worth calculating the total cost across your actual commitment length rather than anchoring on the $2.95 headline figure. If you used the free first-year domain and then cancel inside the 30-day guarantee window, you're also on the hook for the domain's normal registration price.

## Which plan should you choose

- **Choose Mini** if you're launching exactly one small site and don't need room to add more later — it's the cheapest entry point, but the single-website cap means any second project needs a plan upgrade.
- **Choose Start** if you want the flexibility of unlimited websites without paying for Advanced's extra storage headroom — a reasonable default for most small-business or personal-site buyers.
- **Choose Advanced** if you're running multiple sites with meaningfully more media/content, or want more storage buffer before needing to upgrade.
- **Consider managed cloud VPS instead** if you're expecting real traffic growth, need root-level control, or want SPanel's built-in security tooling rather than shared-hosting resource limits.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Free SPanel control panel on VPS avoids per-account cPanel fees | Shared hosting renewal prices jump 3-4x after the intro term |
| Strong Trustpilot reputation (4.9/5 across 2,200+ reviews) | 30-day guarantee excludes domains, SSL and dedicated servers |
| Free daily backups included on shared plans | Mini's single-website limit is restrictive for a starter plan |
| Managed cloud VPS gives a scaling path beyond shared hosting | SPanel has a learning curve if you're used to cPanel workflows |

## Support

ScalaHosting is frequently praised in customer reviews for responsive support, cited repeatedly in Trustpilot feedback as a strength — particularly for VPS customers who need help with server-level configuration rather than basic shared-hosting questions.

## Migration

ScalaHosting reviewers also commonly note smooth website migration assistance as part of onboarding. If you're moving an existing site from another host, that migration support is worth confirming applies to your specific plan and site type before you buy, since scope can vary between shared and VPS migrations.

## Where it's a strong fit

ScalaHosting fits buyers who want a low-cost way into hosting now with a credible upgrade path to managed cloud VPS later, without switching providers. It also suits anyone specifically drawn to SPanel's fee-free model over paying ongoing cPanel license costs on a VPS.

## Where to think twice

If you need the absolute lowest long-term shared-hosting cost and plan to renew indefinitely at list price, the renewal jump from $2.95 to $11.95/month (and similarly on the other tiers) is worth comparing against competitors' renewal rates, not just their intro prices. Buyers who want to stay strictly on cPanel at every tier, including VPS, should also confirm SPanel's feature set covers their workflow first.

## Bottom line

ScalaHosting earns its strong customer reviews mostly on the VPS side, where SPanel offers real cost savings over licensed cPanel and support gets consistently good marks. Shared hosting is competent but unremarkable — cheap to start, expensive-feeling on renewal, and best treated as a stepping stone rather than a permanent home for a growing site.

## FAQs

**Does ScalaHosting use cPanel or SPanel?**
Both, depending on the plan. Shared hosting (Mini, Start, Advanced) runs on standard cPanel. Managed cloud VPS and cloud hosting plans use SPanel, ScalaHosting's own free control panel.

**Is ScalaHosting's advertised price what I'll actually pay long-term?**
No. The $2.95-$9.95/month shared hosting prices are introductory. Renewal rates are $11.95-$19.95/month depending on tier, so factor that into your budget before signing up for a long initial term.

**Does ScalaHosting offer a money-back guarantee?**
Yes, 30 days, covering web, reseller and VPS hosting for new customers. Domains, SSL, dedicated servers and license fees are excluded from the guarantee.

**Does ScalaHosting include a free domain?**
Yes, on Start and Advanced shared hosting plans, for the first year. If you cancel within the 30-day guarantee window, you'll be charged the normal domain price.

**Is ScalaHosting good for beginners?**
Shared hosting with cPanel is approachable for beginners since it's a familiar interface. SPanel on the VPS side is beginner-friendly too, but is a different layout than cPanel, so there's a short adjustment period if you're used to cPanel specifically.

**What does migrating an existing site to ScalaHosting involve?**
ScalaHosting offers migration assistance, and customer reviews frequently mention it going smoothly. Confirm the specific scope of migration support for your plan and site type before purchasing.

**Is ScalaHosting's shared hosting the cheapest option available?**
Its intro prices are competitive but not the lowest on the market, and the renewal pricing is a meaningful multiple of the sign-up rate — it's worth comparing total cost over your intended commitment length against other [Web hosting deals](/category/hosting).

title: SiteGround Review 2026: Pricing, Features and Verdict
excerpt: SiteGround review covering StartUp, GrowBig and GoGeek pricing, renewal costs, features, support and migration to help you decide if it fits your budget.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## SiteGround Review: Is It Worth the Price in 2026?

SiteGround is a solid pick if you value performance and support over the lowest possible price. It runs on Google Cloud, includes free daily backups on every plan, and holds a 4.9/5 rating from over 30,000 Trustpilot reviews. The catch: renewal prices jump 3-4x after your first term, so it suits buyers who plan to stay long-term and don't mind paying more than budget hosts once the intro period ends.

### At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | $3.99/mo (StartUp, first term) |
| Renewal price | $17.99/mo (StartUp) |
| Control panel | Site Tools (proprietary) |
| Uptime | Not independently guaranteed with SLA credits published on the plans page |
| Money-back guarantee | 30 days |
| Free domain | Yes, first year |
| Best for | WordPress sites, buyers prioritizing support and speed over lowest price |

Pricing above reflects rates as of this post's publish date (September 2026) and can change — check SiteGround's own pricing page for the current live rate before buying.

### What SiteGround actually is

SiteGround is a web hosting company founded in Bulgaria in 2004, now operating out of Sofia with additional offices in the US, UK and Spain. It hosts several million domains and is one of a small number of providers officially recommended by WordPress.org. In 2020 SiteGround moved its entire hosting infrastructure onto Google Cloud, running all sites on Google's SSD persistent storage — a detail the company leans on heavily in its marketing, since it's a genuine differentiator from hosts still running older bare-metal or generic cloud stacks.

Instead of cPanel, SiteGround built its own dashboard called Site Tools. It handles domains, email, SSL, backups, staging and site management in one place. It's a cleaner, more modern interface than cPanel for most tasks, but it means some tutorials and third-party guides written for cPanel won't map directly onto SiteGround's layout.

Beyond shared hosting, SiteGround also sells managed WordPress and WooCommerce hosting, and cloud hosting for larger, resource-intensive sites — all built on the same Site Tools panel and Google Cloud backend.

### Pricing table

| Plan | Websites | Storage | Intro price | Renewal price |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| StartUp | 1 | 10 GB | $3.99/mo | $17.99/mo |
| GrowBig | Unlimited | 50 GB | $6.69/mo | $29.99/mo |
| GoGeek | Unlimited | 100 GB | $10.69/mo | $44.99/mo |

All three tiers include free SSL, a free domain for the first year, free daily backups with a 30-day history, a free CDN spanning 170+ locations, and 24/7 support. GrowBig adds on-demand backup copies and staging; GoGeek adds priority support, private DNS and Git-integrated staging — features aimed at developers and agencies managing client sites.

### The real cost breakdown

This is where SiteGround needs a clear-eyed look. The advertised $3.99/$6.69/$10.69 prices only apply to your first billing term (commonly 12 months). After that, plans renew at $17.99, $29.99 and $44.99 per month — a jump of roughly 3.5x to 4.5x over the intro rate. That's a steeper renewal increase than budget-tier hosts like Hostinger or Namecheap, where the multiplier is usually closer to 2-3x.

Practically, that means a StartUp plan costs about $48 for the first year but roughly $216/year every year after, if billed monthly at the renewal rate (annual prepay at renewal typically works out somewhat cheaper per month, but still well above the intro rate). If you're comparing hosts purely on sticker price, run the math on year two and year three, not just the signup screen — SiteGround's actual long-term cost is closer to a mid-tier managed host than a rock-bottom budget provider.

### Which plan should you choose

**Choose StartUp** if you're launching a single small site — a portfolio, a local business page, or a simple blog — and don't expect to add more sites soon. The 1-website cap is the main limitation; if you outgrow it, upgrading later is straightforward but resets your promotional pricing clock.

**Choose GrowBig** if you're running more than one site, want on-demand backup copies you can trigger manually before a risky update, or want staging environments to test changes before pushing live. This is SiteGround's most popular tier for a reason — it removes the single-site ceiling without jumping to GoGeek's developer-focused extras.

**Choose GoGeek** if you're an agency or developer managing multiple client sites, need Git-integrated staging, want priority ticket queues, or require the highest resource allocation SiteGround offers on shared hosting. It's overkill for a single personal site.

### Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Runs on Google Cloud infrastructure | Renewal prices are steep relative to budget hosts |
| Free daily backups included on every plan | StartUp plan caps you at 1 website |
| 4.9/5 rating across 30,000+ Trustpilot reviews | Custom Site Tools panel differs from cPanel-based tutorials |
| Officially recommended by WordPress.org | 30-day guarantee is shorter than some competitors' 45-90 day windows |
| Staging and Git integration on GrowBig/GoGeek | No published uptime SLA credits on the plans page |

### Support

SiteGround offers 24/7 support via live chat and ticket, plus phone support during business hours in several regions. GoGeek customers get access to a priority support queue, which is meant to reduce wait times for agencies managing time-sensitive client work. The high Trustpilot volume and score suggest support quality is a genuine strength rather than just marketing copy — it's one of the more consistently praised aspects across independent reviews.

### Migration

SiteGround provides a free WordPress site migration on GrowBig and GoGeek plans via its Migrator plugin, which handles most standard WordPress transfers automatically. StartUp customers and non-WordPress sites typically need to migrate manually or pay for assisted migration. If you're moving an existing WordPress site and want a hands-off transfer, GrowBig or above is the more practical entry point.

### Where it's a strong fit

SiteGround makes sense if you're hosting a WordPress site and want a provider WordPress.org itself vouches for, if you value daily backups and staging environments without paying extra for them, or if you're willing to pay renewal-tier pricing in exchange for consistently strong support and infrastructure. It's also a reasonable pick for small agencies on GoGeek, given the Git staging and priority support.

### Where to think twice

If your budget is fixed and you're price-sensitive past year one, the renewal jump makes SiteGround one of the more expensive shared-hosting options once the intro term ends — budget hosts with smaller renewal multipliers will cost meaningfully less over a 3-year horizon. The StartUp plan's single-website limit is also worth noting if you might add a second site later, since upgrading forfeits your existing promotional rate.

### Bottom line

SiteGround earns its reputation on infrastructure and support quality, backed by an unusually large and consistently positive review base. But it's not the cheapest option once you look past the first billing cycle — the renewal pricing is a real cost, not a footnote, and it should factor into your decision as much as the storage limits or feature list. If long-term reliability and support matter more to you than shaving a few dollars off monthly hosting, SiteGround is a reasonable choice. If you're optimizing purely for lowest total cost over several years, compare its renewal rates directly against competitors before committing.

See the [SiteGround coupon page](/coupons/siteground) for current offers, or browse [Web hosting deals](/category/hosting) to compare more providers.

### FAQs

**Is SiteGround good for beginners?**
Yes — Site Tools is a clean, guided dashboard, and SiteGround's WordPress installer and staging tools are straightforward even without prior hosting experience.

**Does SiteGround offer a free domain?**
Yes, a free domain is included for the first year on shared hosting plans.

**What happens to my price after the first term?**
Your plan renews at the standard rate — $17.99/mo (StartUp), $29.99/mo (GrowBig) or $44.99/mo (GoGeek) — rather than the introductory price, regardless of how long your initial prepay term was.

**Does SiteGround use cPanel?**
No. SiteGround built its own control panel, Site Tools, which replaces cPanel across all its hosting plans.

**How does SiteGround's migration process work?**
GrowBig and GoGeek customers get a free automated WordPress migration via SiteGround's Migrator plugin; other migrations are typically manual or require a paid migration service.

**What's SiteGround's money-back guarantee?**
30 days from signup, full refund, no long-term contract risk if it isn't a fit.

**Is SiteGround's uptime reliable?**
SiteGround runs on Google Cloud's infrastructure, which is generally associated with strong reliability, though the company doesn't publish a specific uptime SLA with credits on its plans page the way some hosts do.

**Can I upgrade plans later?**
Yes, you can upgrade from StartUp to GrowBig or GoGeek at any time, though doing so typically means paying the new plan's current rate rather than keeping your original promotional price.

## Is HostPapa a good web host?

HostPapa is a solid, mid-priced cPanel host best suited to small-business owners and beginners who want a free website builder, free managed migration, and 24/7 human support bundled in. It's not the cheapest intro price on the market, and renewal jumps are steep, so it fits best if you plan around the long-term cost rather than the headline rate.

| Control panel | cPanel |
