body:
## Is Host IT Smart a good hosting choice?

Host IT Smart is a budget Indian web host offering cPanel shared, reseller and KVM VPS hosting from roughly ₹49/month, with a rare option for month-to-month billing instead of forced annual prepay. It's a reasonable low-cost pick for Indian small sites and WordPress beginners, but independent testing has flagged slower-than-average page speeds, so it's not the choice if raw performance is the priority.

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | ₹49/month (Basic shared, promotional) |
| Renewal price | ₹125/month (Basic, after 3-year term) |
| Control panel | cPanel (shared/reseller), KVM VPS with CentOS/Ubuntu/Debian/AlmaLinux |
| Uptime guarantee | 99.9% (advertised) |
| Money-back guarantee | 30 days |
| Trustpilot rating | 4.4/5 from 196 reviews |
| Best for | Budget Indian shared hosting, small business sites, flexible monthly billing |

## What Host IT Smart actually is

Host IT Smart is a smaller Indian hosting company selling standard cPanel-based shared hosting, reseller hosting and KVM virtual private servers. It doesn't have the brand recognition of Hostinger or Bluehost, and there's comparatively little independent coverage of it — but it does have a real, findable pricing structure, a working Trustpilot profile, and at least one hands-on third-party review (WebsitePlanet), which is more verifiable footing than many small regional hosts offer.

Its main selling point against bigger competitors is billing flexibility: most budget hosts only offer steep discounts if you commit to 12, 24 or 36 months upfront. Host IT Smart advertises plain month-to-month billing on top of its multi-year promotional tiers, which matters if you don't want to prepay years for a site you're still testing.

## Pricing (shared cPanel hosting)

| Plan | Promo price | Disk space | Bandwidth | Websites |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Basic | ₹49/mo | 10 GB NVMe SSD | 10,000 GB | 1 |
| Essential | ₹99/mo | 25 GB NVMe SSD | 25,000 GB | 5 |
| Professional | ₹179/mo | 50 GB NVMe SSD | 1,00,000 GB | 25 |
| Enterprise | ₹399/mo | 100 GB NVMe SSD | 2,00,000 GB | 50 |

Pricing was accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — confirm current rates on Host IT Smart's own pricing pages before buying.

KVM VPS plans sit alongside shared hosting: VPS SM1 starts at ₹299/month (1 vCPU, 4GB RAM, 50GB SSD), scaling up to VPS SM4 at ₹1,465/month (8 vCPU, 32GB RAM, 400GB SSD), all with a dedicated IP and a choice of CentOS, Ubuntu, Debian or AlmaLinux.

## The real cost breakdown

The advertised prices above are promotional, discounted 60-75% off listed rates for an initial term. Host IT Smart's own pricing pages show the Basic shared plan renewing at ₹125/month after a 3-year term, and Essential renewing at ₹250/month — both still well below what most Western hosts charge, but roughly 2-2.5x the headline promo price. Every shared tier includes a free domain and free SSL in the promotional price, which offsets some of the renewal jump if you were going to buy a domain separately anyway. As always with heavily discounted intro pricing, check the exact renewal figure shown at checkout for your billing cycle before committing, since regional pricing and promotions can shift.

## Which plan should you choose

- **Choose Basic** if you're launching a single small site — a blog, portfolio or landing page — and want the lowest entry price.
- **Choose Essential** if you're running up to five sites or want more headroom on storage and bandwidth; Host IT Smart lists this as its most popular tier.
- **Choose Professional or Enterprise** if you're a freelancer or agency hosting many client sites on one account.
- **Choose a VPS plan** if you need root access, better resource isolation, or you're running an application that shared hosting's shared resources can't reliably handle.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Low entry pricing, including a true month-to-month option | Independent testing found page load times slower than the sub-2-second target |
| Standard cPanel with Softaculous one-click installs | One measured uptime test came in below the advertised 99.9% guarantee |
| 24/7 support across live chat, phone, tickets and WhatsApp | No CDN or caching layer included by default |
| Free SSL, free domain and NVMe SSD storage on shared plans | Much smaller track record and review volume than major global hosts |
| KVM VPS option for sites that outgrow shared hosting | Limited independent, up-to-date benchmarking exists beyond a single third-party review |

## Support

Host IT Smart advertises 24/7 support through live chat, phone, ticket system and WhatsApp — a wider channel mix than many budget hosts, which often limit support to tickets only. A third-party review noted response quality was inconsistent in at least one test case, so treat support as generally available but not uniformly excellent until you've tested it with your own account.

## Migration

Host IT Smart's shared plans run standard cPanel, which means migrating an existing cPanel-based site typically works through a normal cPanel-to-cPanel transfer or manual backup-and-restore — the same process that works across most cPanel hosts, rather than anything Host IT Smart-specific. If you're moving off a non-cPanel host (like one running a custom control panel), plan on a manual file and database migration, and confirm with support whether they offer any assisted migration for new signups.

## Where it's a strong fit

Host IT Smart makes sense for Indian users or businesses who want cPanel hosting at a low price point without prepaying multiple years, and who don't need enterprise-grade uptime SLAs or global CDN performance out of the box. The month-to-month billing option is a genuine advantage for testing a new site before committing to a longer term.

## Where to think twice

If your site needs consistently fast global load times, built-in caching/CDN, or you want a host with an extensive independent review history and years of benchmarking data to lean on, Host IT Smart's thinner track record and the performance concerns raised in third-party testing are worth weighing against cheaper-still or more established alternatives.

## Verdict

Host IT Smart is a legitimate, low-cost Indian hosting option with real cPanel and KVM VPS infrastructure, flexible billing, and a respectable Trustpilot score — but it's a smaller player with less independent scrutiny than major hosts, and the one detailed third-party review available flagged real performance gaps against its own advertised uptime. It's a reasonable pick for budget-conscious Indian shared hosting, less so if performance consistency is your top priority.

## FAQs

**Does Host IT Smart use cPanel?**
Yes — shared and reseller plans run standard cPanel with Softaculous for one-click app installs. VPS plans run KVM virtualization with a choice of Linux distributions (CentOS, Ubuntu, Debian, AlmaLinux).

**Does Host IT Smart offer a money-back guarantee?**
Yes, Host IT Smart lists a 30-day money-back guarantee on its shared and VPS hosting plans, per its own pricing pages.

**Is Host IT Smart's promotional price what I'll always pay?**
No. Like most budget hosts, the lowest advertised price applies to a discounted introductory or multi-year term and renews higher afterward — for example, the Basic shared plan renews at roughly ₹125/month after a 3-year term versus its ₹49/month promo price. Confirm the renewal rate for your billing cycle at checkout.

**Can I pay month-to-month with Host IT Smart?**
Yes — unlike many hosts that require an annual or multi-year prepay to unlock their lowest prices, Host IT Smart advertises flexible monthly billing as one of its differentiators.

**Is Host IT Smart good for WordPress?**
It supports WordPress through the standard cPanel/Softaculous one-click installer, which is a common, well-understood setup. It doesn't advertise a purpose-built managed WordPress product with built-in caching, so performance will depend more on plan tier and configuration than on WordPress-specific optimization.

**How is Host IT Smart's uptime and speed in practice?**
Host IT Smart advertises a 99.9% uptime guarantee. An independent third-party test (WebsitePlanet) measured uptime slightly below that figure and found page load times above the commonly cited 2-second benchmark during its test window — treat published guarantees as a starting point and monitor your own site's performance after signup.

**Does Host IT Smart include a free domain?**
Yes, its shared cPanel plans list a free domain as part of the promotional pricing.

**How do I get started with Host IT Smart?**
Pick a shared, reseller or VPS plan on Host IT Smart's website, complete checkout, and your account is typically provisioned automatically. See the [Host IT Smart coupon page](/coupons/hostitsmart) for current offers, or browse [Web hosting deals](/category/hosting) to compare other providers first.

title: IBM Cloud Review 2026: Virtual Server Hosting Pricing
excerpt: IBM Cloud Virtual Servers for VPC reviewed for website hosting: real hourly pricing, free-tier limits, support, migration, and who it actually fits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is IBM Cloud good for website hosting?

This review covers **only IBM Cloud's Virtual Servers for VPC (VSI)** as a way to host a website, plus its free-tier/trial terms — not IBM Cloud's full enterprise catalog of AI, data, and mainframe services. If you're comparing it to a typical shared-hosting or beginner VPS provider, treat IBM Cloud as a developer-oriented infrastructure platform, not a beginner-friendly hosting panel.

### At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Entry-level VM (shared-core, ~2 vCPU/4GB) | ~$45–$70/mo (hourly billed, region-dependent) |
| Free tier | No permanent free VM; $200 credit for 30 days on signup |
| Uptime guarantee | SLA tied to paid support plan, not a blanket public number |
| Money-back guarantee | None beyond the 30-day trial credit |
| Best for | Developers already using IBM/Red Hat tooling, not beginners |

### What IBM Cloud actually is (for hosting purposes)

IBM Cloud is an enterprise infrastructure and platform-as-a-service provider that competes with AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure — its catalog spans AI (Watson), data warehousing, Kubernetes/OpenShift, and IBM Power/mainframe hosting. Somewhere inside that catalog is **Virtual Servers for VPC**, a straightforward IaaS product: you provision a Linux or Windows instance inside a Virtual Private Cloud, attach storage, and manage it yourself over SSH — there's no cPanel, no one-click WordPress installer, and no shared-hosting-style control panel. If you want a website live in ten minutes without touching a terminal, this is the wrong product. If you're a developer who wants raw compute with hourly billing and full root access, it's a legitimate option worth pricing against DigitalOcean, Vultr, and Linode.

### Pricing

Pricing was accurate as of September 2026 and can change — IBM's own calculator requires signing into the console for a live, region-specific quote, so the figures below come from third-party cloud-pricing trackers rather than a fixed published sticker price.

| Profile | vCPU / RAM | Approx. price |
|---|---|---|
| cx2-2x4 (compute, shared-core) | 2 vCPU / 4 GB | ~$0.06–$0.10/hr (~$45–$70/mo) |
| Larger balanced/compute/memory profiles | scales up | Priced per-hour, no flat published table |
| Lite-plan services (non-VSI) | — | Always free, 40+ IBM Cloud services |

### Real cost breakdown

There's no long-term contract to sign and no discounted "intro price" the way shared hosts advertise — Virtual Servers for VPC bill by the hour for exactly what's provisioned, so the real cost is closer to a running total than a fixed monthly fee. A small 2 vCPU/4 GB instance run continuously lands somewhere in the $45–$70/month range depending on region and whether a reserved-instance-style commitment discount applies; stopping the instance when it's not needed reduces the bill accordingly. New accounts get a **$200 credit valid for 30 days**, which is enough to test-drive an instance but not to run a site free indefinitely — after that credit and window expire, billing starts. There is no perpetual free virtual server here, unlike some competitors' always-free compute tiers; the "Lite plan" free tier applies to other IBM Cloud services (Watson APIs, limited Cloud Foundry runtime memory, some storage), not to VSI hosting.

### Which plan should you choose

- **Testing or a short-lived project**: use the $200/30-day trial credit on the smallest shared-core profile — it's enough to prototype and tear down before any charge hits.
- **A low-traffic personal site or dev/staging environment**: an entry-level 2 vCPU/4 GB shared-core instance, stopped when not in use to control the hourly bill.
- **Anything customer-facing or production**: budget for a paid IBM Cloud support plan on top of compute costs — Basic support only covers account and billing issues, not technical help with your server.
- **A first website with no server-admin experience**: this probably isn't the right product — a managed shared host or a beginner-friendly VPS panel will get you live faster with less to manage.

### Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| True hourly, pay-as-you-go billing with no forced long-term contract | No permanent free VM — only a 30-day trial credit |
| Full root access and standard VPC networking/firewall controls | No cPanel/one-click installer — requires server-admin skills |
| Backed by IBM's broader enterprise ecosystem (Kubernetes, Red Hat/OpenShift, hybrid cloud) | Technical support requires a separate paid support plan |
| Useful if you're already standardized on IBM/Red Hat tooling elsewhere | Trustpilot presence is thin and skews negative (see below) |

### Support

Basic IBM Cloud support is included with every account but is limited strictly to account and billing questions — it does not cover troubleshooting your virtual server, your OS, or your application. Getting real technical support (case escalation, faster response SLAs) means subscribing to one of IBM's paid support tiers on top of your compute costs. That's a meaningfully different model from a hosting company where 24/7 live chat is included by default, and it's worth budgeting for if you expect to need help.

### Migration

There's no built-in "migrate my WordPress site" wizard here. Moving an existing site to an IBM Cloud VSI means the same process as moving to any bare IaaS VM: provision the instance, install your stack (web server, database, runtime) yourself or via a script/image, then transfer files and databases over SSH/SCP or a deployment pipeline. If you're coming from a managed shared host, expect a genuinely more hands-on migration than a one-click transfer tool.

### Where it's a strong fit

IBM Cloud VSI makes sense for developers who want hourly-billed, full-root compute and are already working inside IBM's ecosystem — teams running OpenShift/Kubernetes elsewhere on IBM Cloud, or those who need to keep infrastructure inside IBM's enterprise compliance and data-residency footprint. It's also reasonable for short, disposable test workloads that fit inside the $200 trial credit.

### Where to think twice

If you're launching a first website, want a control panel, expect included technical support, or want a genuinely free tier to run a small site indefinitely, look elsewhere. IBM Cloud VSI is not beginner-friendly, and its public reputation on review sites is thin: at the time of writing it shows a low Trustpilot rating from a very small number of reviews, which isn't a reliable statistical signal either way but is worth knowing before you commit production traffic to it.

### Verdict

Scoped narrowly to website hosting, IBM Cloud's Virtual Servers for VPC are a competent, no-frills IaaS product for developers who want hourly billing and root access — not a beginner hosting platform. There's no cPanel, no permanent free instance, and technical support costs extra. If you already use IBM or Red Hat tooling, it's a reasonable place to run a VM; if you're picking your first host for a small site, a purpose-built shared or managed host will get you there with far less setup.

### FAQs

**Does IBM Cloud have a free web hosting plan?**
No. There's no permanent free virtual server for hosting a site. New accounts get a $200 credit for 30 days, and a separate "Lite plan" tier gives always-free access to other IBM Cloud services, but not an ongoing free VSI.

**How much does an entry-level IBM Cloud virtual server cost?**
Third-party pricing trackers put a small shared-core 2 vCPU/4 GB instance at roughly $0.06–$0.10 per hour, which works out to about $45–$70/month if run continuously — check IBM's console calculator for a live, region-specific number since it changes over time.

**Does IBM Cloud include cPanel or a one-click WordPress install?**
No. Virtual Servers for VPC are bare infrastructure — you install and manage your own stack over SSH, similar to a raw AWS EC2 or DigitalOcean Droplet rather than a managed shared host.

**Is IBM Cloud good for beginners?**
Not really. It assumes server-administration knowledge. Beginners looking to launch a first website are usually better served by a managed shared host with a control panel.

**Does IBM Cloud offer 24/7 support?**
Only account/billing help is included by default (Basic support). Technical support for your server or application requires subscribing to a paid IBM Cloud support plan.

**Can I move my existing website to IBM Cloud?**
Yes, but there's no built-in migration wizard — you provision a VSI, install your stack, and transfer your site's files/database manually or via your own deployment tooling.

**Is there a money-back guarantee?**
Not in the traditional sense. Billing is hourly and pay-as-you-go, and new accounts get a $200/30-day trial credit rather than a post-purchase refund policy.

**How does IBM Cloud compare to DigitalOcean or Vultr for hosting?**
DigitalOcean and Vultr are generally simpler to provision and priced with flatter, more predictable monthly plans aimed at developers and small teams. IBM Cloud VSI is comparable in raw compute terms but leans more enterprise, with support and tooling built around larger organizations already using IBM's ecosystem. See our [Web hosting deals](/category/hosting) to compare options, or check the [IBM Cloud coupon page](/coupons/ibmcloud) for current offers.

title: InfinityFree Review 2026: Is Free Hosting Worth It?
excerpt: InfinityFree offers genuinely free web hosting with no ads — but real limits on traffic, storage, email and support. Here's the honest breakdown.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is InfinityFree actually free?

Yes — InfinityFree has one plan, and it costs nothing, forever, with no ads placed on your site. The tradeoff is real limits: 5GB storage, a rough cap of 50,000 daily "hits" (not visitors), no email hosting, and community-only support with no uptime guarantee.

**At a glance**

| | InfinityFree |
|---|---|
| Starting price | $0/month (free forever) |
| Renewal price | $0/month (no paid tier exists) |
| Uptime guarantee | None (99.9% target, not contractual) |
| Money-back guarantee | Not applicable — nothing is charged |
| Best for | Testing, learning, low-traffic personal projects |

## What InfinityFree actually is

InfinityFree is run by iFastNet and is one of the few "free hosting" brands that doesn't use the free tier as a funnel into a paid plan on the same product. There's no checkout page, no upsell during signup, and — unlike a lot of free hosts — no banner or display ads injected into pages your visitors see. You get a working PHP/MySQL hosting account for a real domain or a free subdomain, backed by a Softaculous installer that can one-click WordPress and 400+ other apps.

The honest framing matters here: free hosting isn't a discounted version of paid hosting, it's a different product with different guarantees. There's no service-level agreement on uptime, no guaranteed response time on support, and your account can be paused if it trips a resource limit. If you've read glowing claims that InfinityFree performs like a $10/month host, treat them skeptically — it doesn't, and it was never built to.

## Free plan limits

Pricing was accurate as of this post's publish date and free-tier limits can change — check InfinityFree's own site before relying on any number here.

| Resource | Free plan limit |
|---|---|
| Disk space | 5GB |
| Bandwidth | "Unlimited," capped at ~50,000 hits/24h |
| Files (inodes) | 30,000 max |
| Max file size | 10MB per file |
| MySQL databases | 400 |
| Email accounts | 0 (not available on free plan) |
| PHP / database | PHP 8.3, MySQL 8.0 / MariaDB |
| Control panel | Custom web-based panel (FTP, file manager, phpMyAdmin, cron, DNS) |

## What "free" actually costs you

The dollar cost is zero, but the plan isn't free of tradeoffs. "Unlimited bandwidth" is really a 50,000-hits-per-day ceiling, and a hit isn't a visitor — every image, script and stylesheet request on a page counts separately. A moderately built WordPress page can burn 20-30 hits per load, which puts the realistic ceiling around 100-300 visitors a day before the account gets rate-limited or temporarily suspended.

There's also no email hosting whatsoever on the free plan — not even a single @yourdomain.com inbox. If your project needs business email, you're pairing InfinityFree with a separate mail provider (or Google Workspace) rather than getting it bundled. And because nothing is paid for, there's no support SLA: help comes from a community forum, not a ticket queue with a response-time commitment, and resolution times vary with how active the forum is when you post.

## Is free hosting right for you

Choose InfinityFree if you're prototyping a site, learning PHP/MySQL development, hosting a personal portfolio with light traffic, or running a project where "it might go down and that's fine" is an acceptable answer. The Softaculous installer and phpMyAdmin access make it genuinely usable for real development work, not just a static placeholder page.

Look elsewhere if you're running anything commercial, need guaranteed uptime, expect more than a few hundred visits a day, or need email addresses on your domain. At that point a budget paid host — even an entry-level shared plan — buys you an SLA, support you can escalate, and headroom you won't have to babysit.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Genuinely $0 forever, no hidden upsell | No email hosting at all on the free plan |
| No ads injected into your hosted site | ~50,000 hits/day soft cap, easy to hit with real traffic |
| Softaculous one-click app installer (WordPress, etc.) | No uptime SLA or guaranteed support response |
| 400 MySQL databases, PHP 8.3, phpMyAdmin included | Accounts can be suspended for exceeding limits or inactivity |
| Free subdomain or bring your own domain | 10MB max file size, 30,000 file cap |

## Support

Support is community-based through InfinityFree's own forum rather than live chat, phone, or a ticketing system with a committed response window. Forum threads are actively answered by staff and experienced users, but there's no guarantee of how fast — or whether — a specific issue gets resolved. Treat this as a self-service, best-effort channel, not a substitute for paid support.

## Migration

Moving an existing site in means exporting your files via FTP and your database via a MySQL dump, then uploading through InfinityFree's file manager or FTP client and importing the database through phpMyAdmin — there's no white-glove migration service, since none of this is paid for. Sites already near the 5GB storage or 30,000-file limits may not fit without trimming assets first, so check your current site's size before committing to the move.

## Where it's a strong fit

InfinityFree makes sense for a student project, a personal blog with modest traffic, a portfolio site, or a sandbox to learn PHP and MySQL without any billing risk. It's also a reasonable place to stage a site before pointing a custom domain at paid hosting later.

## Where to think twice

Skip it for anything generating revenue, anything that needs to stay up reliably, or any project where losing access for a day because of a resource-limit suspension would be a real problem. The lack of email hosting alone rules it out for most small businesses.

## Verdict

InfinityFree delivers exactly what it promises: free hosting with no ads and no paid upsell, in exchange for real limits on traffic, storage and support. It's an honest product for the use case it's built for — testing, learning, and low-stakes personal sites — and a poor fit for anything that needs guarantees. If your project outgrows the hits cap or needs email on your domain, compare it against a [Web hosting deals](/category/hosting) entry-level paid plan rather than trying to stretch the free tier further.

## FAQs

**Is InfinityFree really free, or is there a hidden catch?**
It's free with no payment ever required and no ads placed on your site. The "catch" is resource limits — storage, daily hit caps, no email — and no uptime or support guarantees, which is standard for a free product rather than a hidden trick.

**Does InfinityFree limit how much traffic my site can get?**
Yes. Bandwidth is marketed as unlimited, but there's a roughly 50,000-hits-per-24-hours cap, and every asset a page loads counts as a hit. Sites with real traffic can hit that ceiling well before 300 daily visitors.

**Can I use my own domain with InfinityFree?**
Yes — you can point your own domain at an InfinityFree account, or use a free subdomain if you don't have one yet. Domain registration itself isn't included; you'd register it elsewhere and connect it.

**Does InfinityFree include email hosting?**
No. The free plan does not include any email accounts on your domain. You'll need a separate email provider if your project requires business email.

**What happens if my site exceeds InfinityFree's limits?**
Accounts that exceed the daily hit limit, storage quota, or file count can be rate-limited or temporarily suspended until usage drops back under the cap.

**How do I get support with InfinityFree?**
Through InfinityFree's community support forum — there's no live chat, phone line, or committed ticket response time, since the service is free.

**Is InfinityFree good for WordPress?**
It can run WordPress via the Softaculous installer, but the hits-based bandwidth cap and lack of caching/CDN infrastructure make it workable only for low-traffic WordPress sites, not production business sites.

**Should I use InfinityFree for a business website?**
Generally no — the lack of email hosting, no uptime SLA, and traffic ceiling make it a better fit for testing and learning than for a site your business depends on. See the [InfinityFree coupon page](/coupons/infinityfree) for current deal listings, though as a free host there's no discount to find.

title: Leaseweb Review 2026: Dedicated & Cloud Hosting Pricing
excerpt: An in-depth look at Leaseweb's dedicated servers, VPS and cloud pricing, contract terms and support to see if it fits your infrastructure needs.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is Leaseweb a good choice for hosting in 2026?

Leaseweb is a solid pick if you need real dedicated servers, bare metal or cloud infrastructure with global data center coverage — it's not built for beginners wanting a $2/month shared plan. It suits developers, agencies and businesses that need hardware control, custom configurations and predictable global network capacity, not a one-click website builder.

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | ~€3.99-4.99/mo (VPS), dedicated servers from ~$160-180/mo (quote-based) |
| Renewal price | VPS billed monthly, no fixed-term discount cliff; dedicated pricing is configurator-based |
| Uptime guarantee | Network/SLA-backed per product (bare metal, cloud) |
| Money-back guarantee | No blanket guarantee — refund terms vary by product/contract |
| Best for | Developers, agencies and businesses needing dedicated/bare metal or cloud infrastructure |

Pricing above was accurate as of September 2026 and can change — Leaseweb raised new-contract VPS pricing significantly earlier in 2026, so always confirm the live rate at checkout.

## What Leaseweb actually is

Leaseweb is a global infrastructure provider, not a shared-hosting reseller. It runs its own data centers across multiple continents and sells four main product lines: dedicated (bare metal) servers, public and GPU cloud instances, VPS hosting, and colocation/hybrid infrastructure. There's no cPanel or Plesk baked in as a default — everything is managed through Leaseweb's own Customer Portal and a documented Admin REST API, which is exactly what a developer provisioning infrastructure at scale wants, but a step up in complexity from a typical shared-hosting dashboard.

If your mental model of "web hosting" is a shared account running WordPress for a small blog, Leaseweb is the wrong fit — that's what Hostinger or Namecheap are for. Leaseweb makes sense once you're renting real hardware or cloud compute and need to configure the OS, firewall, and network yourself.

## Pricing

| Product | Entry point | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| VPS | ~€3.99-4.99/mo | Smallest tier: around 4 CPU cores, 6GB RAM, 100GB local NVMe storage; billed monthly |
| Dedicated / bare metal | ~$160-180/mo and up | Configured per-spec (CPU, RAM, storage, port speed) rather than sold as flat packages; a Xeon or EPYC box with 32-64GB RAM commonly runs several hundred euros/month |
| Public / GPU cloud | Hourly or monthly | Up to 25% off with a 3-year committed contract |

## Real cost breakdown

Leaseweb's VPS line is the only product with genuinely transparent list pricing, and even that moved during 2026: pricing on new VPS contracts signed from August 1, 2026 onward rose by as much as 49% compared to earlier in the year, driven by memory/storage chip shortages and IP address scarcity. Existing contracts weren't affected, but anyone quoting Leaseweb today should expect current rates to run above older published numbers found in older reviews or forum threads.

Dedicated servers don't have a simple "starting at" sticker price the way VPS does — you pick CPU, RAM, storage and network port through an online configurator, and the total is assembled from there. Independent pricing trackers put a comparable Xeon/EPYC configuration with 32-64GB RAM and a 1-10Gbps port anywhere from roughly $160/month for a lighter config to €800+/month for a heavier EPYC build with NVMe storage and 10Gbps. There's no flat renewal-price jump the way budget shared hosts structure things — you're quoted (and billed) the configured rate directly, though contracts auto-renew for the same term unless cancelled within the notice window.

## Which plan should you choose

Choose VPS if you're running a single application, a staging environment, or a small database workload and want predictable monthly billing without managing physical hardware.

Choose dedicated/bare metal if you need guaranteed, non-shared CPU and I/O performance — a production database, a compute-heavy workload, or compliance requirements that rule out multi-tenant infrastructure.

Choose public or GPU cloud if your workload is bursty or you want hourly billing with the option to scale down, or if you specifically need GPU instances for ML/AI workloads and want a discount for committing to a 3-year term.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Real global data center footprint across multiple continents | Not a beginner-friendly shared host — no one-click WordPress installer |
| VPS plans include DDoS mitigation and free snapshots | No blanket money-back guarantee across all products |
| Dedicated servers fully configurable via online configurator | Dedicated server pricing isn't transparently listed — quote/configure only |
| Admin REST API for infrastructure automation | VPS pricing rose sharply on new contracts starting August 2026 |
| Custom Customer Portal covers SSH keys, reverse DNS, firewall config | Trustpilot rating sits at 3.4/5 — mixed feedback on support response times and billing surprises |

## Support

Leaseweb support is handled through its Customer Portal and standard ticketing channels rather than 24/7 live chat aimed at hosting beginners. Trustpilot reviews describe infrastructure as reliable and support staff as professional once engaged, but also flag delays in response times and occasional unexpected charges — worth budgeting extra time if you're troubleshooting something urgent on a production dedicated server.

## Migration

Moving an existing site or application to Leaseweb means provisioning a new VPS or dedicated server through the Customer Portal, then handling the OS setup, DNS cutover and data transfer yourself (or through your own ops team) — there's no bundled white-glove migration service for typical customers the way some managed shared hosts offer. That's standard for infrastructure-level providers, but it means Leaseweb suits customers who already know how to manage a server, not someone moving a WordPress blog for the first time.

## Where it's a strong fit

- Businesses that need dedicated or bare-metal hardware with full root/OS control
- Teams that want a global data center footprint without managing their own colocation
- Developers comfortable configuring firewalls, SSH access and networking themselves
- Workloads needing GPU cloud capacity with multi-year discount options

## Where to think twice

- Beginners wanting a simple website host with cPanel and one-click installers
- Anyone expecting a straightforward, always-available money-back guarantee
- Budget-sensitive projects where a shared or entry VPS host is genuinely a better fit than dedicated infrastructure
- Buyers who want fully transparent dedicated-server list pricing without going through a configurator or sales quote

## Verdict

Leaseweb earns its place among infrastructure providers for businesses that actually need dedicated servers, bare metal or cloud compute — the hardware options, global footprint and API-driven management are real strengths for that audience. It's a poor match for anyone shopping for cheap shared hosting; the pricing model, contract terms and lack of a one-click control panel all assume you know what you're provisioning. Check current VPS and dedicated pricing carefully before committing, since 2026 saw real rate increases on new contracts.

## FAQs

**Does Leaseweb offer shared cPanel hosting?**
No. Leaseweb focuses on VPS, dedicated/bare metal servers, and public/GPU cloud infrastructure, managed through its own Customer Portal rather than cPanel or Plesk.

**How much does Leaseweb VPS cost?**
Leaseweb's smallest VPS tier launched around €3.99-4.99/month, but pricing on new contracts increased significantly starting August 1, 2026 — confirm the current rate before ordering.

**Does Leaseweb offer a money-back guarantee?**
Leaseweb doesn't advertise a blanket money-back guarantee across all products the way budget shared hosts do. Refund eligibility depends on the specific product and contract, so check the Sales Contract terms for what you're ordering.

**Can I cancel a Leaseweb contract anytime?**
No — Leaseweb contracts auto-renew for the same term as the initial period and can't be cancelled mid-term. Notice periods range from 1 hour (monthly VPS) to 2 months (3+ month contracts), with a 14-day standard notice period under Leaseweb's updated September 2026 terms.

**Is Leaseweb good for beginners?**
Not really. Leaseweb is built for developers and businesses that can manage their own server configuration, OS and networking — it's a poor fit if you want a beginner-friendly, one-click hosting setup.

**How does Leaseweb dedicated server pricing work?**
Dedicated (bare metal) servers are configured per-spec through an online configurator rather than sold as fixed packages, so pricing depends on CPU, RAM, storage and network port speed rather than a flat advertised rate.

**What is Leaseweb's Trustpilot rating?**
Leaseweb holds roughly 3.4 out of 5 on Trustpilot across 300+ reviews, with reviewers citing reliable infrastructure and professional support alongside complaints about response times and billing surprises.

**Does Leaseweb support GPU or AI workloads?**
Yes — Leaseweb offers GPU cloud instances billed hourly or monthly, with discounts of up to 25% available on 3-year committed contracts.

Check the [Leaseweb coupon page](/coupons/leaseweb) for current offers, or browse more [Web hosting deals](/category/hosting) to compare against other providers.

body:
## Is MilesWeb good hosting?

MilesWeb is a solid pick if you're hosting a site aimed at an Indian or APAC audience and want real cPanel access on NVMe storage without paying international-brand prices. It's less compelling if you want a beginner dashboard or don't want to track a renewal jump — the intro price is far from what you'll pay in year two.

| At a glance | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | ₹69/month (Starter, promo term) |
| Renewal price | ₹399/month (Starter) |
| Control panel | cPanel |
| Free domain | Yes, first year |
| Money-back guarantee | 30 days |
| Best for | India/APAC sites wanting cPanel + NVMe on a budget |

## What MilesWeb actually is

MilesWeb is a web hosting company based in India, running shared, reseller, VPS and dedicated hosting aimed primarily at the India/APAC market, with INR pricing and a mix of local and international data centers. Unlike some budget hosts that build a custom control panel, MilesWeb sticks with cPanel — the same interface used by developers and agencies worldwide, so there's no new dashboard to learn if you've hosted anywhere else before.

Its shared hosting lineup runs on NVMe storage across all four tiers, which is a step up from the plain SSD still used by some competitors at similar price points.

## Shared hosting pricing

Pricing below is accurate as of September 2026 and can change — check MilesWeb's own pricing page for the current promotional rate before buying.

| Plan | Intro price | Renewal price | Storage | Websites |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Starter | ₹69/mo | ₹399/mo | 10GB NVMe | 1 |
| Premium | ₹99/mo | ₹499/mo | 50GB NVMe | 25 |
| Business | ₹149/mo | ₹699/mo | 100GB NVMe | 50 |
| Cloud Startup | ₹299/mo | ₹1,499/mo | 150GB NVMe | 100 |

Every tier includes cPanel, a free domain for the first year, and a free SSL certificate.

## The real cost breakdown

MilesWeb's headline prices are promotional-term rates, not what you'll pay indefinitely. The Starter plan's ₹69/month intro price roughly quadruples to ₹399/month on renewal — a jump worth budgeting for rather than discovering at your first renewal invoice. The same pattern holds across every tier: Premium goes from ₹99 to ₹499, Business from ₹149 to ₹699, and Cloud Startup from ₹299 all the way to ₹1,499 per month.

The free domain is only free for the first year; expect a standard domain-renewal charge from year two onward. Because the intro-to-renewal gap is largest on the entry-level Starter plan proportionally, it's worth comparing what you'd actually pay across a full two-year span rather than judging plans purely on the advertised monthly figure.

## Which plan should you choose

Choose **Starter** if you're launching a single small site — a portfolio, a brochure page, or a blog just getting off the ground — and don't need headroom for more domains.

Choose **Premium** if you're running a handful of sites, such as a small agency managing client pages or a business with a main site plus a couple of microsites; 25 websites and 50GB gives real breathing room.

Choose **Business** if you're closer to reseller territory — managing 10+ sites for clients — without yet needing a dedicated reseller plan.

Choose **Cloud Startup** if you want the highest shared-hosting ceiling before stepping up to VPS: 100 websites and 150GB NVMe storage covers most small hosting businesses.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |

| Real cPanel on every tier, not a proprietary dashboard | Renewal prices are several times the intro rate |
| NVMe storage across all shared plans | Entry Starter plan is capped at just 1 website |

| 30-day money-back guarantee | Free domain only covers year one |

## Support

MilesWeb offers 24/7 support channels for hosting customers, which matters most in the India/APAC time zones it's built around — you're not waiting on a support desk aligned to US or European business hours.

## Migration

MilesWeb advertises free website migration assistance for new customers moving from another host, which removes one of the more common friction points when switching providers — you don't need to manually transfer files and databases yourself.

## Where MilesWeb is a strong fit

MilesWeb makes the most sense if your audience or business is based in India or the broader APAC region, you want standard cPanel rather than a custom panel, and you're comfortable budgeting for the renewal price rather than assuming the intro rate is permanent.

## Where to think twice

If you're outside the India/APAC market, want a beginner-simplified dashboard instead of cPanel, or specifically want a host whose promotional and renewal prices stay close together, MilesWeb's pricing structure may not be the best match.

## Verdict

MilesWeb earns its place for India/APAC hosting shoppers who want genuine cPanel access, NVMe storage, and a free domain without international-brand pricing — as long as you go in knowing the renewal rate is the number that actually matters for your second year onward. Check the [MilesWeb coupon page](/coupons/milesweb) for current offers before you sign up, and browse other [Web hosting deals](/category/hosting) to compare against alternatives.

title: MochaHost Review 2026: cPanel Hosting, Pricing & Verdict
excerpt: MochaHost offers cPanel shared, reseller and VPS hosting with free migrations and Windows options — here's the real pricing, features and who it fits.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is MochaHost a good hosting choice?

MochaHost is a solid pick if you want cPanel hosting with free, unlimited site migrations and the option to run Windows Server instead of Linux — useful for ASP.NET sites. It's less compelling if you dislike renewal-price jumps, since its published intro rates are notably lower than what you'll pay on the second term.

## At a glance

| Detail | MochaHost |
|---|---|
| Starting price | ~$3-4/mo (Soho, 1-year term) |
| Renewal price | Reported ~$12-13/mo on entry plans |
| Control panel | cPanel |
| Storage | 30GB (Soho) up to unlimited (Ultimate) |
| Money-back guarantee | 30 days (plans of 1 year+) |
| Best for | Sites needing Windows/ASP.NET or free migrations |

## What MochaHost actually is

MochaHost is a US-based hosting company that's been selling cPanel shared, reseller and VPS hosting for over two decades. Its differentiator versus budget hosts like Hostinger or Bluehost is standard cPanel (not a proprietary panel) plus a genuine choice of Linux or Windows Server at the OS level — most low-cost hosts only offer Linux. It also leans on free, unlimited migrations as a selling point, meaning its support team will move an existing site over from another host at no extra charge, which is a real cost saver if you're switching providers.

The company also pushes a "lifetime" price-lock message in its marketing. Based on what's publicly documented, that refers to a guarantee that your signed-up rate is held for as long as you stay subscribed, rather than a fully free hosting product — it's a price-lock, not free-forever hosting, so don't take the "lifetime free" framing at face value without reading what it actually locks in.

## Pricing table

Pricing was accurate as of this post's publish date and can change — verify current rates on MochaHost's own pricing page before buying.

| Plan | Storage | Sites | Notable extras |
|---|---|---|---|
| Soho | 30GB NVMe SSD | 1 | Free SSL, weekly backups |
| Business | 50GB NVMe SSD | Unlimited | Free domain |
| Mocha | 100GB NVMe SSD | Unlimited | Extra CPU/RAM allocation |
| Ultimate | Unlimited | Unlimited | Free daily premium backups |

## The real cost: intro vs renewal

The entry-level Soho plan lists an introductory rate in the roughly $3-4/month range when you prepay a one-year term. That's competitive against other budget cPanel hosts. The catch — and it's a real one — is the renewal rate. Multiple independent pricing trackers report Soho-tier renewals landing around $12-13/month, which is roughly triple the intro price. That's a steeper jump than some competitors, so budget for the second-year bill rather than assuming the sign-up price holds. If MochaHost's "lifetime discount" price-lock applies to your specific plan and term, it may soften this — but confirm the exact terms at checkout, since third-party pricing pages don't always reflect the live offer.

There's no verified evidence of domain or email add-on costs beyond what's typical for cPanel hosts, and a free domain is included starting at the Business tier for the first term.

## Which plan should you choose

Choose **Soho** if you're launching a single small site or blog and want the lowest entry price — just budget for the renewal jump.

Choose **Business** if you're running more than one site or want a free domain bundled in; the jump from Soho to Business also unlocks unlimited sites, which is usually worth the small price increase.

Choose **Mocha** if your site needs more CPU/RAM headroom — a growing WooCommerce or membership site, for example — without moving to a full VPS.

Choose **Ultimate** if you want unlimited storage and the highest resource ceiling MochaHost offers on shared hosting, or if you're hosting several resource-heavier sites under one account.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| cPanel included (not a proprietary panel) | Renewal pricing rises sharply versus intro rate |
| Free, unlimited migrations | Storage caps on lower tiers (30-100GB) |
| Windows Server option for ASP.NET sites | Fewer independent uptime benchmarks than larger hosts |
| 30-day money-back guarantee on annual+ terms | Advanced caching/CDN features not confirmed as standard |
| NVMe SSD storage across plans | Shorter/monthly terms may not carry the same refund window |

## Support

MochaHost offers support through the usual mix of ticketing and live channels available on its site, plus phone contact for sales and account questions. Trustpilot reviewers frequently single out support responsiveness and staff helpfulness as a strength, with many reviews naming individual support agents by name for resolving issues quickly. That said, reviews are mixed rather than universal — at least one documented case involved an account suspension over a disputed charge that caused extended downtime, so support quality can vary by situation.

## Migration

Free migration is one of MochaHost's more concrete advantages: its team will move an existing cPanel-based site over at no charge, which directly saves the fee some competitors (like Bluehost or HostGator) charge for the same service. Reports suggest the migration tool handles smaller sites cleanly, while larger WordPress installs with lots of plugins or custom configuration may need manual follow-up from support. If you're moving a complex site, it's worth opening a support ticket ahead of time to confirm what the migration will and won't cover automatically.

## Where MochaHost is a strong fit

- You need Windows Server hosting for an ASP.NET or .NET-based site, which many budget hosts simply don't offer.
- You're switching from another cPanel host and want the migration handled for free instead of paying a transfer fee.
- You want a standard cPanel interface rather than learning a host's proprietary dashboard.
- You're comfortable budgeting for a renewal price increase rather than assuming the sign-up rate is permanent.

## Where to think twice

- You want the lowest possible long-term cost — the renewal jump on entry plans works against that.
- You need heavy-duty caching, a built-in CDN, or advanced performance tooling as a standard shared-hosting feature — MochaHost hasn't confirmed these as included by default.
- You want a large, independently benchmarked track record — MochaHost has less third-party performance testing coverage than the biggest-name hosts.

## Verdict

MochaHost earns its keep on two specific strengths: it gives you real cPanel (not a proprietary substitute) with a genuine Windows Server option, and it backs that with free, unlimited migrations that save real money if you're switching hosts. The trade-off is a renewal price that climbs well above the intro rate, so it rewards buyers who read the fine print and budget for year two rather than those chasing the lowest possible sign-up number. For a Windows/ASP.NET site or a straightforward cPanel migration, it's worth a look; for the absolute cheapest long-term shared hosting, compare renewal rates against other providers first.

## FAQs

### Does MochaHost use cPanel?

Yes — MochaHost runs standard cPanel across its shared, reseller and most Linux-based plans, rather than a custom-built dashboard.

### Does MochaHost offer Windows hosting?

Yes, MochaHost offers Windows Web Hosting and Windows VPS options alongside its Linux plans, which is useful for ASP.NET or other Windows-dependent applications.

### Is MochaHost's migration really free?

MochaHost advertises free, unlimited migrations handled by its support team. Reports suggest this works smoothly for smaller sites, while larger or more complex WordPress installs may need extra manual steps — confirm scope with support before a big migration.

### What does "lifetime free" actually mean with MochaHost?

Based on publicly available information, MochaHost's lifetime messaging refers to a price-lock guarantee that holds your signed-up rate rather than a fully free hosting product. It is not literally free-forever hosting, so read the specific terms for your plan.

### Does MochaHost have a money-back guarantee?

MochaHost states a 30-day, no-questions-asked money-back guarantee on plans of one year or longer. Confirm whether the same window applies if you choose a shorter monthly term.

### How much does MochaHost renew at after the first term?

Renewal pricing is reported to be substantially higher than the intro rate — some entry-plan trackers show renewals landing several times above the sign-up price. Check the exact renewal figure at checkout before buying, since it varies by plan and term length.

### Is MochaHost good for beginners?

MochaHost's use of standard cPanel means the learning curve is similar to most established hosts, and features like free SSL and automatic backups reduce manual setup work for a first-time site owner.

### Where can I find current MochaHost deals?

Check the [MochaHost coupon page](/coupons/mochahost) for current offers, and browse [Web hosting deals](/category/hosting) to compare it against other providers.

title: NameHero Hosting Review 2026: Pricing, Speed & Verdict
excerpt: NameHero review covering cPanel + LiteSpeed performance, real intro vs. renewal pricing, support, migration and whether it's worth choosing in 2026.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is NameHero good hosting?

NameHero is a solid pick if you want cPanel hosting with real LiteSpeed performance instead of the Apache stack most budget hosts still run. It suits WordPress sites, agencies and anyone who's outgrown ultra-cheap shared hosting, though its lowest advertised prices require a 3-year commitment and jump considerably at renewal.

| At a glance | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | From roughly $2-3/month on a 3-year term (promotional) |
| Renewal price | Around $10.95/month (Starter Cloud) up to $34.95/month (Business Cloud) |
| Control panel | cPanel |
| Web server | LiteSpeed (with Redis and MariaDB) |
| Money-back guarantee | 30 days (minus an $8.95 setup fee) |
| Best for | WordPress sites, agencies, small businesses wanting cPanel + speed |

## What NameHero actually is

NameHero is a US-based hosting company running shared, reseller and VPS hosting out of a Kansas City data center, plus an EU location for international customers. Its shared and reseller lineups use cPanel/WHM as the control panel and LiteSpeed as the web server — a combination that tends to outperform the Apache-based stacks that still ship on many cheaper hosts, particularly for dynamic WordPress sites with caching enabled. NameHero markets its infrastructure as environmentally conscious: independent reviews describe its Kansas City facility as built underground in a former limestone mine, which provides natural temperature control, alongside stated renewable-energy partnerships. That's a genuine efficiency angle worth noting, though it's not the same as a third-party-certified carbon-neutral claim, so treat it as a marketing point rather than a verified certification.

## NameHero pricing

Pricing below reflects NameHero's plan structure as of this post's publish date and can change — always confirm current rates on NameHero's own pricing page before buying.

| Plan | Positioned for | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Starter Cloud | Single small site | Lowest entry price, 1/2/3-year terms only |
| Plus Cloud | Growing sites, more storage headroom | 1/2/3-year terms only |
| Turbo Cloud | Multiple sites, higher traffic | Available monthly too |
| Business Cloud | Agencies, resource-heavy sites | Available monthly, highest renewal tier |

Storage is advertised as unlimited across shared tiers, but NameHero caps inode counts (roughly 250,000 files/emails/objects) on the two lowest plans — a limit that mostly matters if you're hosting large mailboxes or sites with huge numbers of small files, not a typical single-site WordPress install.

## The real cost: intro vs. renewal

NameHero's cheapest headline price only applies on the longest (3-year) term, paid upfront, and it steps up meaningfully at renewal — Starter Cloud renews around $10.95/month and Business Cloud around $34.95/month, based on NameHero's published renewal rates. That's a common shared-hosting pattern, not unique to NameHero, but it means the advertised "from $X/month" figure isn't what you'll pay long-term. Two- and three-year signups do include a free domain registration or transfer, which offsets some of that gap in year one. Budget for the renewal rate, not the promo rate, when comparing hosts.

## Which plan should you choose

Choose Starter Cloud if you're launching a single small site and want the lowest entry cost, accepting the inode ceiling. Choose Plus Cloud if you need more breathing room but still run just one or two sites. Choose Turbo Cloud if you're running several sites, want monthly billing flexibility, or need more consistent performance under traffic. Choose Business Cloud if you're an agency or resource-heavy site that needs the highest resource allocation NameHero's shared/cloud tier offers.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| LiteSpeed + cPanel combo, generally faster than Apache-based budget hosts | Lowest tiers only sold on 1-3 year terms, no monthly option |
| Free SSL and one free website migration included | Renewal pricing is a significant step up from intro pricing |
| High Trustpilot rating with a large review volume | Inode caps on the two cheapest plans can bite email-heavy sites |
| 30-day money-back guarantee on hosting plans | Refund reduced by a non-refundable setup fee, one refund per customer lifetime |

## Support

NameHero offers live chat and ticket-based support, along with a self-serve help center covering setup and troubleshooting articles. Independent reviews and its strong Trustpilot rating suggest support response times are a genuine strength rather than a marketing line — worth weighing if responsive human support matters more to you than the absolute lowest price.

## Migration

NameHero includes one free website migration with its shared hosting plans, handled by its team rather than left entirely to the customer. That covers moving an existing site's files, database and email from another host, which removes a common point of friction when switching providers — though it's worth confirming exactly what's included (number of sites, email accounts) before you commit if your setup is complex.

## Where NameHero is a strong fit

NameHero fits well for WordPress site owners and small agencies who want genuine LiteSpeed performance under cPanel without moving to VPS, and who are comfortable prepaying a longer term to get the lowest rate. It's also a reasonable choice for anyone specifically prioritizing US-based cPanel hosting with a data center that markets itself on efficiency.

## Where to think twice

If you want month-to-month billing on the cheapest plans, or you're hosting a mailbox-heavy site that could bump into the inode caps on Starter or Plus Cloud, look elsewhere or budget for a higher tier. Anyone allergic to renewal-price jumps should also read the fine print before locking into a 3-year term.

## Verdict

NameHero earns its reputation as a faster-than-average cPanel host thanks to its LiteSpeed stack, and its Trustpilot numbers back up consistently positive support experiences. The catch is the same one that applies across most of the shared-hosting industry: the eye-catching entry price needs a long prepaid term and renews considerably higher, so the real decision point is whether NameHero's renewal rate still beats the alternatives you're comparing it against once the honeymoon pricing ends.

## FAQs

**Does NameHero use cPanel?**
Yes — NameHero's shared, reseller and VPS hosting all run on cPanel/WHM rather than a proprietary panel.

**What web server does NameHero use?**
LiteSpeed, paired with Redis and MariaDB on shared plans, which is typically faster than the Apache stack many budget hosts still run.

**Does NameHero offer a money-back guarantee?**
Yes — a 30-day money-back guarantee on Web Hosting, Reseller Hosting and VPS Hosting, minus a non-refundable $8.95 setup fee, limited to one refund per customer.

**Is NameHero's storage really unlimited?**
Storage is marketed as unlimited, but the two cheapest shared plans cap inode counts around 250,000 — a limit on file/email object counts rather than raw disk space.

**Does NameHero's price go up at renewal?**
Yes. The lowest advertised prices apply to the 3-year term and step up at renewal — Starter Cloud renews around $10.95/month and Business Cloud around $34.95/month based on NameHero's published rates.

**Does NameHero help migrate my existing site?**
Yes — shared hosting plans include one free website migration handled by NameHero's team.

**Is NameHero actually a green host?**
NameHero markets efficiency features like an underground data center with natural cooling and stated renewable-energy partnerships, but this is a company claim rather than an independently certified carbon-neutral rating, so treat it as a positive detail rather than a guarantee.

**Can I pay monthly with NameHero?**
Only on the Turbo Cloud and Business Cloud tiers — Starter and Plus Cloud are sold on 1-, 2- and 3-year terms only.

Compare current offers on the [NameHero coupon page](/coupons/namehero), or browse more [Web hosting deals](/category/hosting) before you decide.

title: NxtGen Review 2026: Enterprise Cloud & Colocation India
excerpt: NxtGen review 2026: India's sovereign cloud and colocation provider for enterprises — data centers, IaaS pricing, DR services, and who it's really built for.
author: Editorial Team
body:
## Is NxtGen good for enterprise cloud and colocation?

NxtGen is a solid pick for Indian enterprises that need sovereign, India-resident infrastructure — colocation, cloud IaaS or disaster recovery — but it isn't built for solo site owners or small budgets. Pricing is quote-based, sales cycles are longer, and the value shows up in compliance, density and support, not a low advertised monthly rate.

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting price | Quote-based (entry cloud IaaS referenced around ₹4,999/month by resell partners) |
| Renewal price | Negotiated per contract, not a fixed published rate |
| Uptime guarantee | Not publicly published as a flat SLA number; SLAs are set per contract |
| Money-back guarantee | None published — enterprise contract terms, not a retail refund window |
| Best for | Indian enterprises needing colocation, sovereign cloud, or DR/BCP infrastructure |

Pricing above was accurate as of September 2026 and can change — always confirm current figures directly with NxtGen before signing anything.

## What NxtGen actually is

NxtGen (NxtGen Datacenter & Cloud Technologies) is a Bengaluru-headquartered infrastructure provider, not a consumer web host. Its data center campuses in the Bengaluru region are built as high-density facilities (HDDC — High Density Datacenter), engineered to exceed Tier III specifications, with capacity across multiple independent buildings for up to roughly 2,000 high-density racks.

The company's product lines split into four areas:

- **Colocation and dedicated hosting** — single-rack through full server-hall deployments, with remote-hands support.
- **Enterprise cloud IaaS** — branded Elastic Cloud Services / SpeedCloud, offering virtualized compute, NVMe storage and software-defined networking (VMware NSX-based).
- **Disaster recovery and business continuity** — backup and DR services aimed at regulated industries.
- **Managed security, CDN and, more recently, AI infrastructure** — GPU/AI-oriented capacity has been added to the portfolio as demand for India-resident AI compute has grown.

NxtGen markets itself specifically on data sovereignty: as an Indian entity, it argues it sits outside the reach of foreign data-access laws (like the US CLOUD Act) that can apply even to Indian regions of US-headquartered hyperscalers. That pitch is aimed squarely at regulated enterprises — banking, government-adjacent, and compliance-heavy sectors — not hobby sites.

## Pricing — mostly quote-based, not self-serve

There is no public retail price list for NxtGen's colocation or higher-tier cloud services. Rack space, cloud VM sizing (vCPU/RAM/storage/network), and DR contracts are all scoped and quoted individually based on what a customer actually needs.

| Service | Pricing model | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Colocation / dedicated racks | Custom quote | Scoped to rack density, power draw, and contract length |
| Elastic Cloud IaaS | Referenced from ~₹4,999/month by authorized resellers | Final cost scales with vCPU, RAM, NVMe storage and bandwidth |
| Disaster recovery / BCP | Custom quote | Priced against RPO/RTO requirements |
| AI/GPU infrastructure | Custom quote | Newer offering, capacity-dependent |

That ₹4,999/month entry figure comes from an authorized NxtGen reseller's public pricing page rather than NxtGen's own site, so treat it as a rough floor rather than a guaranteed rate — get a direct quote before budgeting against it.

## Real cost breakdown

Because nearly everything is negotiated, there's no fixed intro-vs-renewal price structure the way there is with retail shared hosting. What you can plan around instead:

- **Entry cloud IaaS**: reseller-listed from roughly ₹4,999/month for a base configuration, scaling up with more vCPU, RAM and storage.
- **Colocation**: priced per rack unit or per rack, with density (kW per rack) and power redundancy driving cost more than storage/bandwidth does.
- **Contract terms**: enterprise agreements typically run longer than a monthly retail term, and NxtGen does not publish a standard money-back window — refund and cancellation terms are set in the individual contract, so get them in writing before committing.

## Which plan should you choose

- **Choose managed colocation** if you already own hardware and need Tier III-class rack space, power density and remote-hands support in India rather than a hyperscaler region.
- **Choose Elastic Cloud IaaS / SpeedCloud** if you want on-demand virtualized compute without owning hardware, and value India-resident data over the broadest global footprint.
- **Choose the DR/BCP service** if your primary need is a compliant backup and business-continuity site rather than production infrastructure.
- **Choose the AI/GPU infrastructure line** if you need India-resident GPU capacity for training or inference workloads and can't or don't want to use an offshore cloud region.

## Pros and cons

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Genuine India-resident, sovereign-cloud positioning for regulated workloads | No public, fixed pricing — everything above entry cloud tiers is quote-based |
| High-density data centers (HDDC) built to exceed Tier III spec | Not built for small sites, solo developers or tight self-serve budgets |
| Broad product line: colocation, cloud, DR, security, CDN, AI infrastructure under one vendor | Limited independent customer review coverage (small sample on Gartner Peer Insights, no Trustpilot presence found) |
| Multiple independent facilities in the Bengaluru region for redundancy | Longer sales/procurement cycle than a self-serve cloud sign-up |

## Support

NxtGen positions itself around named account managers and India-based support rather than a ticket queue — the kind of support model enterprise colocation and cloud customers typically expect, with remote-hands service available for colocation racks. There's no public live-chat-for-everyone consumer support desk; support is arranged as part of the account relationship, so ask about response-time SLAs during the sales process rather than assuming a specific number.

## Migration

Moving into NxtGen — whether racking existing hardware in colocation or migrating workloads onto its cloud IaaS — is handled as a scoped onboarding project rather than an automated one-click migration tool. Expect a technical discovery call, a migration plan tailored to your existing environment (especially if you're moving off AWS/Azure/GCP), and coordinated cutover windows for anything DR- or compliance-sensitive. Budget real project time for this; it isn't a same-day switch the way spinning up a new shared-hosting account is.

## Where it's a strong fit

NxtGen is a strong fit for Indian enterprises and regulated organizations that specifically need data to stay on Indian soil, that want colocation in a high-density Tier III-class facility, or that want a domestic alternative to a hyperscaler for cloud IaaS, DR or emerging AI/GPU workloads.

## Where to think twice

If you're running a personal blog, a small business website, or anything that fits comfortably on shared or budget cloud hosting, NxtGen is the wrong tool — there's no self-serve low-cost tier, no website builder, and the sales process is built around enterprise procurement, not a five-minute signup.

## Verdict

NxtGen earns its place as a genuine enterprise infrastructure option for Indian businesses that care about data sovereignty, high-density colocation, or a domestic cloud/DR alternative to the big three hyperscalers — its facilities and product breadth back that up. What it isn't is a budget host: there's no published price list for most services, procurement takes longer, and independent customer review volume is thin outside employer-review sites. Get a direct quote scoped to your workload before comparing it against anything else.

## FAQs

**Is NxtGen a shared hosting provider?**
No. NxtGen is an enterprise infrastructure provider — colocation, cloud IaaS, disaster recovery and data center services — not a consumer shared-hosting brand with website builders or one-click app installs.

**How much does NxtGen cost?**
Most services are quote-based. An authorized reseller lists entry-level cloud IaaS from around ₹4,999/month, but colocation, DR and higher cloud tiers are priced per contract based on your requirements.

**Does NxtGen offer a free trial or money-back guarantee?**
NxtGen doesn't publish a standard consumer-style money-back guarantee. Refund and cancellation terms are set in the enterprise contract, so confirm them directly before signing.

**Where are NxtGen's data centers located?**
NxtGen's High Density Datacenter (HDDC) facilities are located across multiple independent buildings in the Bengaluru, India region.

**Is NxtGen good for AI/GPU workloads?**
NxtGen has expanded into AI infrastructure services, offering India-resident GPU capacity as an alternative to offshore cloud regions for training and inference workloads — availability and pricing are quote-based.

**What does "sovereign cloud" mean for NxtGen?**
NxtGen markets itself as an Indian entity operating outside the reach of foreign data-access laws that can apply to Indian regions run by US-headquartered hyperscalers, which matters for regulated or compliance-sensitive customers.

**How reliable is NxtGen based on independent reviews?**
NxtGen holds a 4.5-star rating from a small sample (4 reviews) on Gartner Peer Insights' managed hybrid cloud hosting category as of this review; no meaningful Trustpilot presence was found for the company, so treat review coverage as limited rather than extensive.

**How do I get started with NxtGen?**
Since pricing and configuration are quote-based, the process starts with contacting NxtGen's sales team to scope your colocation, cloud or DR requirements rather than a self-serve signup.

Looking for lower-cost, self-serve hosting instead of enterprise infrastructure? Check the [NxtGen coupon page](/coupons/nxtgen) for any current offers, or browse [Web hosting deals](/category/hosting) for budget-friendly alternatives.

## What Oracle Cloud actually is (for hosting purposes)

That's the trade for the free compute — it suits developers and technically comfortable site owners, not someone who wants a one-click WordPress install with support on standby.

## Pricing: Always Free tier and paid Compute tiers
